# Addon anatomy

**Status:** GA
**Version checked:** 2026-10-28
**Technical owner:** Platform Engineering (ADK)
**Last reviewed:** 2026-11-16

## Manifest

`manifest.json` is validated as manifest v2 by `kassis-addon check`. The host runs the same check when it inspects a package and when it loads an addon, and only when `manifestVersion` is `2`. A failure uses the same KADK code as `check`. A manifest without that version keeps the previous inspect and load path. The fields an addon author sets most often:

| Field                                          | Role                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`                                           | Addon id. Routes mount at `/api/v1/addons/<id>`.                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `signing`                                      | Optional `{ alg: "ed25519", keyId }`. `keyId` is the sha256 hex of the Ed25519 SPKI DER. It is inside the signed body. A first-party manifest that still has no `signing` block verifies with the kassis current key. |
| `tier`                                         | `1` (default) or `2`. See [Tiers](./tiers.md).                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `routing.mountPath`                            | Path the host passes into `initialize()`.                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `database.ownedTables` / `database.readAccess` | Tables this addon owns or may read. Do not use a wildcard for a new addon.                                                                                                                                            |
| `permissions`                                  | Catalog entries (`{ name, displayName, … }`) in the addon permission namespace. On enable, the host registers them in core RBAC the same way it used to for v1 `definedPermissions`. The RBAC configuration screen lists them under the addon id; an administrator assigns them to roles (nothing is granted automatically). See [Permission namespaces](../addons/permission-namespaces.md). |
| `groups`                                       | Optional RBAC groups (`name`, `displayName`, `permissions[]`). Each name stays in the addon namespace; each permission must be declared in `permissions`. The host creates them empty at install (S2.12).                                             |
| `process.packs[]`                              | Optional list of pack files under `process/`. Each entry is `{ key, kind, file }`. The key stays in the addon namespace (`<id>.case.application`). The file matches `schema/process-pack.schema.json`: `name`, `references` (other pack keys, never ids), `permissions`, `resourceTypes`, and a `body` object. `kassis-addon check` rejects a key outside the namespace, a dangling reference, an undeclared permission or record type, and a file that is missing or not listed. Kinds and the host-schema gap are in `process-pack-kinds.json`. Every current kind has `schema: null` (no published JSON Schema on the template or rule row), so check warns KADK-313 and does not validate `body`. On install and update the host installs every kind in `process-pack-kinds.json` as a draft (S2.53, S2.54), in that file's order. Case templates resolve flow and lifecycle keys to ids. Provenance columns are set. List and entity templates are left inactive, rules and prompts and emails are left disabled, and a template that has a publish flag stays unpublished. An unknown kind fails the install. An update whose body changed adds a new draft and leaves the previous row, so a running case stays on the ids it started with. A clone has empty provenance and is not updated or removed. Uninstall deletes unused rows; a row a case still references is kept with `retired_at` set and an audit row. Disable does not change these rows. Studio and Settings show “Provided by addon” and Clone. Null provenance still means administrator-authored (release step `20261116-process-pack-provenance`). |
| `extends`                                      | Optional list of `ctx.extend` extension point ids the addon registers (for example `documentable`, `auditSubject`, `investigationDomain`). The host refuses a registration not named here. Tier 2 may use waves 1–6 on the tier matrix. |
| `resourceTypes[].sensitivity`                  | Codex seal level: `standard`, `confidential`, or `mnpi`. Required on every `resourceTypes` entry when `database.ownedTables` is non-empty (KADK-124). |
| `ui.entryFile`                                 | Frontend bundle entry, usually `index.js`.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `ui.runtimeLoad`                               | When true, the host loads the page from the runtime catalog instead of a static import.                                                                                                                               |
| `mcp.tools`                                    | Tool names. Tier 2 tools are forwarded. They are not imported into the host.                                                                                                                                          |

## initialize()

The loader calls `initialize()` with the platform host, the database handles, config, secrets, a logger, and `ctx`. `ctx` is the [addon context](../addons/addon-context-facades.md). Addons are not required to read `ctx`, but new code should.

Register HTTP with `host.registerRoute({ mountPath, handler })`. `mountPath` comes from the manifest. Register callable features with `host.registerCapability`. Callers use `getCapability` and must keep working when the capability is absent.

## Frontend register()

`frontend/index.ts` must export a function named `register`. The runtime loader calls `mod.register` or `mod.default.register`. It also reads `routes`. Without `register`, the page can load and still show no widgets.

```ts
import { registerExampleExtensions } from './register';
export { registerExampleExtensions };
export const register = registerExampleExtensions;
```

User-visible chrome goes through the addon i18n helpers. See [Frontend i18n](../addons/frontend-i18n.md). Do not import `i18next` from an addon.

An addon built outside this repository keeps `@kassis/host-sdk` and `@kassis/addon-ui` external. For rung 2 and 3, `kassis-addon init` copies `vite.config.mjs`. The UI entry is `src/ui/index.ts`. The bundle is `frontend/dist/index.js`. `ui.entryFile` is `index.js`, relative to that folder. The config reads externals from `@kassis/addon-sdk/browser-externals.json`. The host serves those modules from `/host-sdk/`.

## Template

`kassis-addon init` copies `templates/kassis-addon` and fills `publisher`, the addon id, and tier.

| Path                            | Role                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `manifest.json`                 | Tier 2 unless publisher `kassis` passes `--tier=1`. `hostApi` is `^1.0.0`. Tier 2 includes `resources.memoryMb` (128) and `health.path` (`/health`); the supervisor refuses a tier 2 addon without memory. `entrypoints.main` is `dist/server/index.js`. `signing` is omitted until `sign`. A publisher other than `kassis` cannot use tier 1, and the id is prefixed with `<publisher>-` when it does not already start with that prefix. Declares `audit.actions`, `events.publishes` (with `events/*.schema.json`), `jobs.types`, and `prompts.keys` for the names exercised in `test/server.test.ts`, so offline tests match what the host enforces. |
| `package.json`                  | `build`, `build:server`, `build:ui`, `test`, `check`, and `certify`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `tsconfig.json`                 | Typecheck for `src`. It does not emit JavaScript.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `src/server/index.ts`           | `defineAddon({ initialize })` from `@kassis/addon-sdk`. The host still calls the exported `initialize`. A record type passed to `defineRecordType` requires `canAccess`, `onDelete`, `sensitivity` (`standard`, `confidential`, or `mnpi`), and `auditSubject`. A manifest slice with a non-empty `database.ownedTables` requires `data.retention`. Missing one of those is a type error. `check` reports KADK-124 (sensitivity) and KADK-309 (retention) for the same manifest rules. |
| `src/ui/index.ts`               | `routes` and `register`. Copied for rung 2 and rung 3.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `frontend/dist/index.js`        | UI bundle. `ui.entryFile` is `index.js` inside this folder. Present after build when the rung has a UI.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| `test/server.test.ts`           | Calls `createTestContext({ manifestPath })` from `@kassis/addon-testkit`. No database; undeclared facade names fail like the host.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `migrations/`                   | Rung 3 only. Each `*.up.sql` has a `*.down.sql`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `.github/workflows/certify.yml` | Installs, builds, tests, checks, and certifies.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `REQUIREMENTS.md`               | Structured requirements (YAML front matter, `FR-*` / `NFR-*` rows, scaffold examples). Replace with your BRD for real addons.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `PLAN.md`                       | One rung per requirement row: `configuration`, `extension-point`, `facade`, `own-code`, or `gap`. `kassis-addon plan` writes the split to `.kassis/evidence/requirement-mapping.json`. `certify` fails when a row has no rung.                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `GAPS.md`                       | Blocked Must requirements and the platform capability needed to unblock them. Naming a Must id here satisfies `kassis-addon requirements`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `TEST-REPORT.md`                | Platform prerequisite checks (P1–P3) and acceptance test evidence (AT-*).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `.gitignore`                    | `dist`, `frontend/dist`, `.kassis/evidence`, `node_modules`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |

Rung 1, the default, is the server only. Rung 2 adds the UI. Rung 3 adds the UI and `migrations/`. `npm run build` prints `dist/server/index.js` and, when the UI entry exists, `frontend/dist/index.js`. The build fails when `initialize` is missing, and when the UI was built and `register` is missing. The server bundle is ESM and leaves `@kassis/*` external. The UI bundle leaves the modules in `browser-externals.json` external.

## Changelog

| Date       | Change                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 2026-11-16 | `importQuestionnairePack` keeps its domain-and-kind reuse and now records a disposer. Disable retires a pack that call created and leaves a reused pack in place (S2.26). |
| 2026-11-16 | Pack update adds a new draft when the body changes and leaves the previous row. Clone clears provenance. Uninstall deletes unused rows and sets `retired_at` on rows a case still uses, with an audit event. Release step `20261116-process-pack-retired`. Studio and Case Lifecycle settings show the addon label and Clone (S2.55). |
| 2026-11-16 | `kassis-addon check` and `certify` fail a manifest v2 addon whose `canAccess` returns true or only throws, or whose `onDelete` is empty or only throws (KADK-729–732). `scaffold record-type` throws from both handlers until they are replaced. Enable uses the same rule. |
| 2026-11-16 | Install and update also create list, entity, dashboard and data-flow templates, policy, flag, QA and compliance rules, and questionnaire, prompt and email templates as drafts. Existing `source_key` rows are left unchanged. `importQuestionnairePack`, `registerPromptPack` and `registerInvestigationTemplate` stay on the host (S2.54). |
| 2026-11-16 | Install and update create kind-1 process packs as drafts: case template, flow template and lifecycle policy. Pack keys resolve to ids. Provenance columns are set. Nothing is published. Other kinds fail the install until they have an installer (S2.53). |
| 2026-11-16 | `process.packs[]` and `process/*.json` are the process pack format. `kassis-addon check` validates keys, references, permissions and record types offline. No kind has a host JSON Schema yet; those gaps are recorded in `process-pack-kinds.json` and warned as KADK-313 (S2.52). |
| 2026-11-16 | Release step `20261116-process-pack-provenance` adds nullable `source_addon`, `source_key` and `source_version` on core template and rule tables for future process packs (S2.51). After `20261027-list-schema`, `public.list_templates` and `public.policy_rules` are views over `addon_list_management`; the step alters those base tables and rebuilds the views. Apply the step before a backend that writes those columns. |
| 2026-11-16 | `kassis-addon plan` maps each requirement row in `PLAN.md` and writes `.kassis/evidence/requirement-mapping.json`; `certify` fails on KADK-720/721/722 (S2.48). |
| 2026-11-16 | `kassis-addon requirements` traces Must rows in `REQUIREMENTS.md` to `test/` or `GAPS.md` and writes `.kassis/evidence/requirements-coverage.json`; `certify` fails on KADK-719 (S2.39). |
| 2026-11-16 | `kassis-addon scaffold --kind=record-type` emits `defineRecordType` with access, delete, sensitivity and retention stubs, wave 1 `ctx.extend` registrations, and four failing tests the author must replace (S2.20). |
| 2026-11-16 | SDK `defineAddon` and `defineRecordType`: a record type requires `canAccess`, `onDelete`, `sensitivity`, and an audit subject; owned tables require `data.retention` at the type level. The template entry uses `defineAddon` (S2.17). |
| 2026-11-16 | RBAC role editor groups manifest-registered permissions under the addon id (`permissions.category`); assignable in the picker without automatic role grants (S2.10). |
| 2026-11-16 | Host install creates manifest `groups[]` as empty core RBAC groups (`groups.owner_addon`). Update reconciles the permission list and keeps members. Uninstall removes the groups, memberships and direct grants (S2.12). |
| 2026-11-16 | Optional manifest `groups[]`: namespaced group slugs and permission lists validated like `requiredPermissions` (KADK-122, KADK-123). |
| 2026-11-16 | Manifest v2 adds `extends[]` and fixes `resourceTypes[].sensitivity` to `standard`, `confidential`, or `mnpi`; sensitivity is required when `database.ownedTables` is set (KADK-124). |
| 2026-11-16 | Package inspect and addon load refuse a `manifestVersion: 2` manifest with the same KADK code as `kassis-addon check`.                                              |
| 2026-11-16 | Integration proof (`templateAddonPermissionProof.integration.test.ts`): template v2 permissions register in RBAC and gate addon routes instead of `system.admin` (B13 / S1.04). |
| 2026-11-16 | Route and MCP gates read manifest v2 `permissions` objects (`{ name }`) for mount-level checks, not only string entries (B13 / S1.03).                               |
| 2026-11-16 | Tier 1 and tier 2 start paths register manifest v2 `permissions` objects in the core permission catalog (B13 / S1.02).                                            |
| 2026-11-16 | The template manifest declares audit, event, job, and prompt names used in `test/server.test.ts`, plus `events/started.schema.json` for the sample publish call.   |
| 2026-11-16 | `createTestContext` reads the manifest and refuses undeclared facade names with the same KADK codes as the host. See [Testing](./testing.md).                    |
| 2026-11-16 | `init` copies `REQUIREMENTS.md`, `GAPS.md`, and `TEST-REPORT.md` shaped after BRD-ADK-001, including scaffold-kind requirement examples.                            |
| 2026-10-28 | The tier 2 template sets `resources.memoryMb` to 128 and `health.path` to `/health`. The host refuses a tier 2 addon without memory.                                |
| 2026-10-28 | Manifest v2 may carry `signing.keyId`, covered by the signature.                                                                                                    |
| 2026-10-28 | `ui.entryFile` is `index.js`, relative to `frontend/dist`. A path with a slash is KADK-504. The catalog strips a leading `frontend/dist/`.                          |
| 2026-10-28 | The template server bundle is `dist/server/index.js`. The UI bundle is `frontend/dist/index.js`. Rung 1 is server only, rung 2 adds UI, and rung 3 adds migrations. |

# AI agents

**Status:** GA
**Version checked:** 2026-10-28
**Technical owner:** Platform Engineering (ADK)
**Last reviewed:** 2026-11-19

## Coding-agent profile

The signed profile `addon-coding-agent` (version 2) ships inside `@kassis/addon-cli`. `sync --profile=addon-coding-agent` checks that signature and writes:

- `.kassis/agent-profile.lock.json`
- `AGENTS.md`
- `.cursor/rules/adk-guardrails.mdc`
- `.claude/CLAUDE.md`
- `.github/copilot-instructions.md`

Version 1 remains bundled for verification. Its signature still verifies. The version 2 document also keeps that version on `previousVersion`, which is what `GET /api/v1/agent-registry/profiles/published/addon-coding-agent` returns.

Version 2 replaces the machine check `kassis-addon-certify` on `adk.certify` with `kassis-addon-check`, `kassis-addon-conformance`, `kassis-addon-build` and `kassis-addon-test`. Certify runs those checks and writes the only copy of the results. An agent does not type them into the attestation.

An unsigned version 3 draft ships in the CLI package pending sign/publish (decision D7). Repository paths for profile files are in [Maintainers](./maintainers.md). Every blocking guardrail in that draft names a machine check. `adk.requirements-traced` is backed by `kassis-addon requirements` (KADK-718 and KADK-719). `adk.requirement-plan-mapped` is backed by `kassis-addon plan` (KADK-720, KADK-721, and KADK-722). `adk.sdk-imports-only` and `adk.reversible-migrations` use `kassis-addon conformance`. `adk.event-schemas-and-null-capabilities` uses `kassis-addon check` for schema paths (KADK-406); that command does not scan source for a null capability. `adk.attest-pinned-profile` reads the lock and `.kassis/attestation.json`. `adk.certify` still names check, conformance, build, and test. Guardrails with no machine check are advisory: `adk.work-in-own-repo`, `adk.declared-permissions-and-audit`, `adk.declare-widened-access` (the evidence pack still shows the change summary), `adk.no-unrequested-refactors`, `adk.lowest-rung`, and `adk.document-changes`. The draft also has six coding skills (`adk.add-route`, `adk.add-table`, `adk.add-event`, `adk.add-job`, `adk.add-ui-page`, `adk.add-mcp-tool`) whose bodies live under `kassis-skills/adk-add-*/SKILL.md`. `adk.mandatory-contract-intact` is a blocking machine guardrail on that unsigned draft. Certify records the check and fails a `return true` or throw-only `canAccess` (KADK-730), an empty or throw-only `onDelete` (KADK-732), a missing access check for a declared record type (KADK-729), and a missing deletion handler when the addon owns tables (KADK-731). The record-type scaffold only throws from those two handlers, so a fresh scaffold fails the check until they are replaced. The signed profile does not include this guardrail yet. Do not point `sync` at the draft until a person signs it (decision D7). The signed version 2 profile is unchanged and still self-attests those blocking rules. Certify records the machine check ids in `.kassis/evidence/checks.json`.

`sync --instance=<url>` downloads `GET /api/v1/agent-registry/profiles/published/<id>` instead of the bundled file.

Group A reuse checks run inside `kassis-addon check`: banned packages are listed in `@kassis/addon-sdk/banned-dependencies.json` (KADK-221), and approval, notification, audit, user, and role tables fail unless `REUSE.md` explains them (KADK-310, warning KADK-311). Each other owned table needs `database.tableNotes` (warning KADK-312).

The guardrail catalogue is `@kassis/addon-sdk/guardrails.json` (group, level, check, KADK code, fix hint). `kassis adk sync` writes catalogue metadata into `AGENTS.md` and related agent rule files. `kassis-addon certify` uses the catalogue fix hint when a guardrail fails with its primary KADK code.

Group D soft budgets (`adk.thin-addon-budgets`) are machine-checked by `kassis-addon budgets` (KADK-723 when over a limit without a `BUDGETS.md` reason). Group E engineering checks (`adk.outbound-timeouts`, `adk.pagination-and-query-caps`, `adk.ui-i18n`, `adk.idempotent-handlers`, `adk.no-module-state`) are machine-checked by `kassis-addon engineering` (KADK-724–728). Certify records those check ids in `.kassis/evidence/checks.json`. They are not yet on the signed coding profile or the unsigned v3 draft (`inProfile: false`); adding them is a human profile update (D7).

`npx kassis-adk-mcp` is a stdio MCP server. Messages are newline-delimited JSON. Project tools: `validate_manifest`, `run_checks`, `explain_error`, and `scaffold`. Offline discovery tools (packaged data, no network): `list_facades`, `get_facade`, `list_extension_points`, `list_events`, `get_event_schema`, `get_tier_matrix`, `list_guardrails`, `get_guardrail`, `search_docs`, `get_example`, and `find_core_feature` (maps a common need to the core feature, facade or extension point, and an example). Optional live mode against `GET /api/v1/adk/catalog` waits on that catalog route (S2.36).

## Registry, runs, and attestation

An API key whose scopes include `agent.service` is an agent principal. Mutating MCP tools require a run id. `certify` can start a run and post attestation answers when `KASSIS_ADK_INSTANCE`, `KASSIS_ADK_TOKEN`, and `KASSIS_ADK_AGENT_ID` are set.

Audit rows for an agent call include `agentId`, `runId`, `model`, `promptKey`, and `promptVersion` on both the success path and the rejection path.

## Final decisions

The hidden investigation update tool is marked `finalDecision`. When the agent's autonomy says the call must be approved, or the run is not attested, the runtime does not execute the tool. It creates an approval request through the existing approvals path and returns that request id. The maker sees it in Atelier under Your requests. Approving the request does not apply the tool: the `mcp_final_decision` record type has an empty `onApproved` handler.

Autonomy is read from the agent profile. If it cannot be read, the level is the most restrictive one (`suggest`).

## Settings

| Key                                           | Meaning                                                                                      |
| --------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `agents.autonomy.levels`                      | Per-agent autonomy. Unreadable values fall back to suggest.                                  |
| `agents.autonomy.attestationFailureThreshold` | Failures inside the window that downgrade the agent to suggest.                              |
| `agents.autonomy.windowMinutes`               | Window for the failure count. The count is stored in the agent registry, not in one process. |
| `agents.autonomy.budgetLimit`                 | Spend limit for an agent principal.                                                          |
| `agents.autonomy.callCost`                    | Cost reserved before a tool call.                                                            |

`agent_config_draft` returns a proposed settings change with `applied: false`. It does not write. A person publishes configuration.

## Changelog

| Date       | Change                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 2026-11-19 | Client docs name bundled profiles and `npx kassis-adk-mcp`; repository profile paths are [Maintainers](./maintainers.md).                    |
| 2026-11-16 | Unsigned v3 draft guardrail `adk.mandatory-contract-intact` (KADK-729–732). Certify and enable refuse return-true, empty, and throw-only record contract handlers. Signing remains D7. |
| 2026-11-16 | Group D/E machine checks: `kassis-addon budgets` (KADK-723) and `kassis-addon engineering` (KADK-724–728); catalogue rows flipped/added with `inProfile: false` pending D7 profile update. |
| 2026-11-16 | Unsigned profile v3: every blocking guardrail names a machine check. `adk.work-in-own-repo`, `adk.declared-permissions-and-audit`, `adk.declare-widened-access`, and `adk.no-unrequested-refactors` are advisory. Signing remains D7. |
| 2026-11-16 | Core feature map MCP tool `find_core_feature` (packaged `core-features.json`: need → feature, facade/extension, example). |
| 2026-11-16 | Group A reuse checks in `kassis-addon check`: banned dependencies (KADK-221), private mechanism tables (KADK-310/311), owned-table notes (KADK-312). |
| 2026-11-16 | Guardrail catalogue `guardrails.json` in the SDK; MCP `list_guardrails` / `get_guardrail`; certify and sync read catalogue metadata. |
| 2026-11-16 | Unsigned coding profile v3 draft: `adk.requirements-traced` machine guardrail and six `adk.add-*` coding skills. Signing remains D7 / human-only. |
| 2026-11-16 | Offline discovery tools: `list_facades`, `get_facade`, `list_extension_points`, `list_events`, `get_event_schema`, `get_tier_matrix`, `search_docs`, `get_example`. |
| 2026-10-28 | The dev MCP server speaks newline-delimited JSON and exposes `validate_manifest`, `run_checks`, `explain_error`, and `scaffold`.              |
| 2026-10-28 | Coding profile version 2 replaces the `kassis-addon-certify` machine check with check, conformance, build and test. Version 1 stays readable. |

# CLI reference

**Status:** GA
**Version checked:** 2026-10-28
**Technical owner:** Platform Engineering (ADK)
**Last reviewed:** 2026-11-19

Run `npx kassis-addon <command>` after installing `@kassis/addon-cli`. The packed CLI is a bundle. `npx kassis-adk-mcp` starts the MCP server from the same package. Help and errors name the command `kassis-addon`. `--help` exits 0. `--version` prints the CLI version and exits 0. `--flag value` and `--flag=value` both work. `--json` on every command prints `{ "ok", "issues", "data" }`. An issue is `{ "code", "severity", "message", "fix", "file", "line" }`. An unknown command prints usage and exits 1. Exit 0 is success. The MCP server also exposes offline discovery tools (`list_facades`, `get_facade`, `list_extension_points`, `list_events`, `get_event_schema`, `get_tier_matrix`, `search_docs`, `get_example`, `find_core_feature`) that read packaged kit data with no network.

| Command              | Flags                                                         | What it does                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `init`               | `--id` `--dir` `--publisher` `--tier` `--rung`                | Copies `templates/kassis-addon`. `--id` is required. Publisher defaults to `kassis`, tier to 2, rung to 1. Tier 1 is refused unless the publisher is `kassis`. Any other publisher gets an id prefix of `<publisher>-` when the id does not already start with it. Rung 1 is server only. Rung 2 adds UI. Rung 3 adds UI and migrations.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `build`              | `--only=server` or `--only=ui`                                | Writes `dist/server/index.js`. Also writes `frontend/dist/index.js` when `src/ui/index.ts` exists. Prints each path. Exits 1 when `initialize` is missing, or when the UI was built and `register` is missing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `check`              | `--json`                                                      | Validates `manifest.json` against manifest v2. Schema errors use the existing KADK-1xx codes. A permission outside `<id>.` is KADK-110. Also refuses a banned dependency (KADK-221) and a private approval, notification, audit, user, or role table (KADK-310). An explained `REUSE.md` row warns with KADK-311. An owned table with no `database.tableNotes` warns with KADK-312. Writes `.kassis/evidence/reuse-core.json`. When `process.packs[]` is set, checks each `process/*.json` offline: namespace (KADK-125), missing file (KADK-126), key or kind mismatch (KADK-127), undeclared permission (KADK-128), undeclared record type (KADK-129), unresolved reference (KADK-314), envelope (KADK-316), duplicate key (KADK-317), unlisted file (KADK-318). A kind with no host schema warns KADK-313 and does not check `body`. For manifest v2, a missing record access check is KADK-729, a `return true` or throw-only access check is KADK-730, a missing deletion handler on owned tables is KADK-731, and an empty or throw-only deletion handler is KADK-732. The record-type scaffold fails this until those handlers are filled in. Writes `.kassis/evidence/mandatory-contract.json`. |
| `conformance`        | `--json`                                                      | Runs the addon-testkit import check on `src/`, `frontend/`, and built `dist/server/index.js` and `frontend/dist/index.js` when those files exist. Also rejects an up script with no down script.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `test`               | `--json`                                                      | Runs `node --test` in `./test`. Prints `No test directory` and exits 0 when that folder is missing.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `dev`                | `--image` `--json`                                            | Starts a local container with Docker or Podman. The image is `--image`, then `KASSIS_DEVHOST_IMAGE`, then `~/.kassis/devhost.json`, then `ghcr.io/kassis-ai/kassis-devhost:latest`. It pulls that image when it is not local. The addon directory is mounted read-only at `/opt/kassis/dev-addon` and the port is published on 127.0.0.1. It also starts a tier 2 runner container on an internal network and does not mount a Docker socket. It does not build an image.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `migrate`            | `up` `down` `status` `--target` `--json`                      | Runs only against the database of the dev host started by `dev`. If that host is not running, it refuses. `--target` is refused unless it is that same database.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `doctor`             | `--requirements` `--json`                                     | Checks that Node is 20 or newer, that `npm ping` reaches `https://registry.npmjs.org/`, that a key file exists under `~/.kassis/keys`, that `KASSIS_ADK_INSTANCE` answers `GET /api/v1/adk/version`, and that `manifest.hostApi` accepts `HOST_API_VERSION`. With `--requirements`, scans `src/`, `frontend/`, `test/`, and built `dist/server/index.js` for `ctx` facade calls refused at the manifest tier (`tier-matrix.json`); issues use KADK-219.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `requirements`       | `--json`                                                      | Parses Must rows in `REQUIREMENTS.md` and requires each `FR-*` / `NFR-*` id to appear in a file under `test/` or in `GAPS.md`. Writes `.kassis/evidence/requirements-coverage.json`. Untraced Must ids use KADK-719; a missing `REQUIREMENTS.md` uses KADK-718. `certify` runs the same gate before the attestation check.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `plan`               | `--json`                                                      | Reads every `FR-*` and `NFR-*` row in `REQUIREMENTS.md` and requires a rung in `PLAN.md`: `configuration`, `extension-point`, `facade`, `own-code`, or `gap`. Writes `.kassis/evidence/requirement-mapping.json` with counts per rung. A missing `PLAN.md` is KADK-720, an unmapped id is KADK-721, and a bad or duplicate rung is KADK-722. `certify` runs the same gate.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `budgets`            | `--json`                                                      | Soft thin-addon budgets: owned tables, `routes.mount` calls, production dependencies, and server source bytes. Over a limit needs a `BUDGETS.md` reason row. Writes `.kassis/evidence/thin-addon-budgets.json`. Missing reasons are KADK-723. `certify` runs the same gate and records check id `adk.thin-addon-budgets`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `engineering`        | `--json`                                                      | Scans addon source for outbound calls without timeouts (KADK-724), `findMany` without `take`/`skip` (KADK-725), UI chrome outside i18n or `i18next` imports (KADK-726), non-idempotent job/event handlers (KADK-727), and module-level `let`/`var` state (KADK-728). Writes `.kassis/evidence/engineering-practice.json`. `certify` runs the same gate and records the five check ids.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `scaffold`           | `--kind` `--id` `--name` `--dir`                              | `--kind=addon` is init. The other kinds add a route, capability, event, job, migration, UI slot, UI page, or MCP tool in the current addon. `scaffold route` writes `src/server/routes/<name>.ts`, adds the permission, depends on `express`, and calls the mount helper from `initialize`. `scaffold job` writes `src/server/jobs/<name>.ts` and registers the handler from `initialize`. `scaffold event` writes `src/server/events/<name>.ts`, `schemas/<name>.schema.json` with required fields, and `events.publishes` in the manifest. `scaffold migration` writes `migrations/<nnnn>_<name>.{up,down}.sql`, sets `data.schema`, adds a qualified row to `database.ownedTables`. Install and update apply those scripts for a tier 2 package. `scaffold ui-slot` and `scaffold ui-page` add `ui.contributions.nav`, write `src/ui/pages/<name>.tsx` using `@kassis/host-sdk`, `src/ui/locales/en.json` and `fr.json`, wire the page into `src/ui/index.ts`, and add `test/ui/<name>Page.render.test.ts` (requires rung 2 or 3). `scaffold mcp-tool` declares `contributions.mcp` with `dist/mcp/contribution.js`, writes `src/mcp/tools/<name>.ts` via `@kassis/mcp-contract`, wires `src/mcp/contribution.ts`, and adds `test/mcp/<name>.mcp.test.ts`. `scaffold capability` adds `<id>.<name>` version `1.0.0` to `provides` for tier 1 and tier 2. |
| `pack`               | `--out=<dir>` `--json`                                        | Writes an evidence pack after certify would pass: attestation, lock, certify result, `index.json` and `README.md`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `sbom`               | `--json`                                                      | Writes `sbom.json` for the libraries this addon ships. Versions come from `package-lock.json`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `package`            | `--out=<path>` `--json`                                       | Writes `<id>-<version>.addon` beside the addon folder (or at `--out`). The file is a zip of the signed `manifest.json`, the files in the content-hash scope, `frontend/dist/` when that folder exists, the certify evidence pack (`checks.json`, `attestation.json`, and `agent-profile.lock.json`), and `sbom.json`. It writes `sbom.json` when that file is missing or older than the server build. It prints the file path and the sha256 of the zip. It refuses a manifest with no signature or no `contentHash`, and a folder whose certify checks did not all exit 0. It does not sign and it does not call the network. Sign again after `sbom.json` changes. |
| `deploy`             | `--instance=<url>` `[file.addon]` `--json`                    | Uploads the `.addon` to `POST /api/v1/addon-security/deploy` and prints the approval request id. `--instance <url>` and `--instance=<url>` both work. The token is `KASSIS_ADK_TOKEN`. The optional field `archiveSha256` is the sha256 of the uploaded bytes. The same command works from a jump host that only has the `.addon` file.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `status`             | `--instance=<url>` `--json`                                   | Prints the installed version and pending staged versions from `GET /api/v1/platform/addons/installations`. The token is `KASSIS_ADK_TOKEN`. Each row is the addon id, active version, publisher, and pending versions.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| `rollback`           | `--instance=<url>` `<addon-id>` `<target-version>` `--json` | Calls `POST /api/v1/platform/addons/<addon-id>/rollback` with `{ "targetVersion": "<target-version>" }`. The token is `KASSIS_ADK_TOKEN`, sent as a bearer token and not printed. The addon id must match the manifest id pattern. The version must be `x.y.z`. HTTP 200 switches the active version and prints the addon id and version. HTTP 202 holds the request for approval when the target widens access and prints the approval request id. A redirect is refused. Exit 0 on success and 1 on failure. The route requires `system.admin`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `sign`               | `--key=<path>` `--json`                                       | Signs this addon. With `--key`, writes `contentHash` and `signing.keyId`, then the signature. Refuses a key file inside the addon folder. Inside the repo, without `--key`, uses the repo signer for the manifest id and does not add `signing`. Outside the repo, `--key` is required.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| `keys generate`      | `--publisher=<id>` `--json`                                   | Writes an Ed25519 private key to `~/.kassis/keys/<fingerprint>.key` (mode 0600; on Windows, only the current user). Prints the fingerprint and the public key. The private key is not written into the addon folder.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `keys export-public` | `--key=<path>` `--out=<path>` `--json`                        | Writes the SPKI DER hex of that private key.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `keys register`      | `--instance=<url>` `--publisher=<id>` `--key=<path>` `--json` | POSTs the public key to `/api/v1/platform/addon-publishers/<id>/keys`. Token: `KASSIS_ADK_TOKEN`. The instance still has to approve the key.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| `certify`            | `--json`                                                      | Runs check, conformance, build, test, requirements tracing, requirement mapping, soft budgets, and engineering practice; writes `.kassis/evidence/checks.json` (machine check ids `adk.requirements-traced`, `adk.requirement-plan-mapped`, `adk.attest-pinned-profile`, `adk.thin-addon-budgets`, and the five group E check ids); then checks the attestation. KADK-714 blocks a blank outcome. KADK-715 warns when machine evidence is typed in. Untraced Must ids also emit KADK-718/719. A missing or invalid plan emits KADK-720/721/722. Budgets emit KADK-723; engineering emits KADK-724–728. The mandatory record contract emits KADK-729–732 and records check id `adk.mandatory-contract-intact`. A fresh `scaffold record-type` fails that check because `canAccess` and `onDelete` only throw. The same run applies the group A reuse checks (KADK-221, KADK-310, KADK-311, KADK-312). `--json` prints `{ "ok", "issues", "data" }` and still exits 1 when `ok` is false. |
| `attest`             | `--json`                                                      | Writes `.kassis/attestation.json` from the lock when it is missing, then prints its path. It does not post to the registry. `certify` posts when the instance env vars are set.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `explain`            | `<code>` `--json`                                             | Prints the meaning of a KADK code.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `sync`               | `--profile=<id>` `--instance=<url>` `--from=<file>` `--json`  | Verifies the signed profile, reads `--from`, or downloads `GET /api/v1/agent-registry/profiles/published/<id>`, then writes the lock and the rule files.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| `rules`              | `--json`                                                      | Rewrites `AGENTS.md` and the rule files from the lock. Fails if you have not run `sync`.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |

`sync --instance` reads the published profile route. The id is a slug such as `addon-coding-agent`, not a database number. The response body is `{ success, data }`. The CLI uses `data`.

Example:

```bash
npx kassis-addon init --id=sample-tprm-check --publisher=kassis --dir=../sample-tprm-check
npx kassis-addon certify --json
```

# Addon Development Kit

**Status:** GA
**Version checked:** 2026-10-28
**Technical owner:** Platform Engineering (ADK)
**Last reviewed:** 2026-11-19

The Addon Development Kit (ADK) is how a Kassis addon is created, checked, signed, and loaded. It is also how an AI coding agent is given a signed profile, and how an operator turns an addon on.

Client-facing pages in this section describe published npm packages and `kassis-addon`. They intentionally omit kassis repository paths so the same docs work when the kit lives in **kassis-adk**. People who build or ship the kit from the kassis monorepo use [Maintainers](./maintainers.md).

## Who it is for

- **Addon developers** build a tier 1 or tier 2 addon and ship it with `kassis-addon`.
- **AI coding agents** follow the signed `addon-coding-agent` profile. `sync` writes the lock file and the rule files the agent must attest to.
- **Operators** enable addons, apply release seeds, and install an air-gapped bundle.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph host [Host]
    loader[Addon loader]
    caps[Capability registry]
    ui[UI runtime load]
    mcp[MCP runtime]
    registry[Agent registry]
  end
  agent[Agent principal]
  t1[Tier 1 addon]
  t2[Tier 2 supervisor]
  child[Tier 2 child process]
  loader --> t1
  loader --> t2
  t2 --> child
  t1 --> caps
  child --> caps
  ui --> t1
  ui --> child
  agent --> mcp
  mcp --> registry
  mcp --> caps
```

Tier 1 addons run in the host process. Tier 2 addons run in a child process and do not need their own entry file. The host forwards their HTTP routes and MCP tools. In-repo addon pages load from the host bundle through `/runtime-addons.json`. An addon built outside the repository leaves `@kassis/host-sdk` and `@kassis/addon-ui` external, and the host serves those modules from `/host-sdk/`. Agent principals call MCP tools through the agent registry, which can turn a final decision into an approval request. Approving that request does not run the tool.

## Reading order

1. [Install](./install.md)
2. [Quickstart](./quickstart.md)
3. [Addon anatomy](./addon-anatomy.md)
4. [Tiers](./tiers.md)
5. [CLI reference](./cli-reference.md)
6. [Testing](./testing.md)
7. [Signing and trust](./signing-and-trust.md)
8. [Publishing](./publishing.md)
9. [AI agents](./ai-agents.md)
10. [Operators](./operators.md)

Kit maintainers in the kassis repository: [Maintainers](./maintainers.md).

Related pages that this guide does not copy:

- [Addon context facades](../addons/addon-context-facades.md)
- [Semver policy](../addons/semver-policy.md)
- [Frontend i18n](../addons/frontend-i18n.md)
- [Permission namespaces](../addons/permission-namespaces.md)
- [KADK error codes](../reference/adk-error-codes.md)
- [Addon deploy CLI](../addons/addon-deploy-cli.md)

## Changelog

| Date       | Change                                                                                              |
| ---------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 2026-11-19 | Named **Platform Engineering (ADK)** as technical owner. Client pages avoid repository paths (S3.11). |

# Install

**Status:** GA
**Version checked:** 2026-10-28
**Technical owner:** Platform Engineering (ADK)
**Last reviewed:** 2026-11-19

## Prerequisites

- Node.js 20 or newer (`kassis-addon doctor` checks the runtime).
- Docker or Podman when you want `kassis-addon dev` against a local dev host image.

## Packages

The packages an addon installs are `@kassis/addon-sdk`, `@kassis/addon-testkit`, `@kassis/addon-ui`, `@kassis/host-sdk`, `@kassis/agent-kit`, and `@kassis/addon-cli`. They are public on npmjs.com under the `@kassis` scope, so `npm install` needs no token. A project `.npmrc` with `@kassis:registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/` keeps the scope on npmjs.com when a global `.npmrc` maps `@kassis` somewhere else.

Depend on `@kassis/addon-sdk` at `^0.1.0`. That is the kit npm line. It is not the host API. `manifest.hostApi` stays `^1.0.0`. The version rules are in the [semver policy](../addons/semver-policy.md). `@kassis/adk-core` and `@kassis/mcp-contract` share that kit line. Install the CLI for commands. An addon that scaffolds an MCP tool depends on `@kassis/mcp-contract`.

The packages in the install command below build to `dist` in the published tarball. `@kassis/addon-sdk`, `@kassis/addon-testkit`, `@kassis/agent-kit`, and `@kassis/addon-cli` ship JavaScript. `@kassis/host-sdk` and `@kassis/addon-ui` ship type declarations plus a small JavaScript shim so plain Node can import the package. The shim does not contain the host UI. The running host serves `@kassis/host-sdk` at `/host-sdk/index.js` and `@kassis/addon-ui` at `/host-sdk/addon-ui.js`. An addon frontend build leaves those imports external.

```bash
npm install @kassis/addon-sdk @kassis/addon-testkit @kassis/addon-ui @kassis/host-sdk @kassis/agent-kit @kassis/addon-cli
```

Published tarballs request [provenance](./publishing.md) when installed from the registry.

## CLI

Install `@kassis/addon-cli` and run `npx kassis-addon`. `--version` reads that package's own `package.json`. The MCP server is `npx kassis-adk-mcp`. The package bundles the addon template, manifest schema, signed coding profiles, and the public verification key. It does not contain a private signing key. `sign` without `--key` exits 1 unless your environment supplies a host signer.

## Air-gapped bundle

Download the kit air-gap bundle from your release channel (checksums and signatures ship with the bundle). Extract it to a directory such as `./airgap`. Install dependencies with `file:` tarballs listed in `checksums.txt` and verify hashes before use. The bundle includes the SDK, testkit, template, public verification key, `sbom.json`, and the six public package tarballs. It refuses to include a private signing key.

After install, run `npx kassis-addon init` and the [Quickstart](./quickstart.md) flow without the npm registry.

Kit maintainers who build the bundle from the kassis repository use [Maintainers](./maintainers.md).

## Changelog
