# Operators

**Status:** GA
**Version checked:** 2026-10-28
**Technical owner:** Platform Engineering (ADK)
**Last reviewed:** 2026-11-19

## Enable and disable

Enable and disable go through the platform lifecycle API (`system.admin`), not a Settings toggle. See [Addons overview](../../business/addons/overview.md).

The UI kill switch is `@kassis/addon-ui`. A killed addon renders the killed slot and does not mount its page. A thrown slot shows the failed-slot message and the rest of the host stays up.

Addon pages that set `ui.runtimeLoad` load from `/runtime-addons.json` (hashed files, not cached) or, in dev, from `/addons-ui/<id>/<file>?contentHash=<hash>`. The host serves that URL only after the addon passed the signature gate on its last load and is still enabled, and only while the content-hash and UI-hash fingerprints still match. First-party addons (`kassis`, `kassis-corp`, or an empty publisher) do not need `uiContentHash`. The browser imports addon entries by URL, so Vite does not link their CSS. Each `/runtime-addons.json` entry is `{ js, css }`, where `css` lists the stylesheets of the entry chunk and of the chunks it imports statically. In dev, the library build writes all addon CSS to `frontend/dist/index.css`, and the `addons/ui-catalog` endpoint lists the CSS files at the root of `frontend/dist` as `styleFiles`. The loader links those stylesheets and waits for them before it imports the entry. Unload removes them. The loader skips a disabled addon. Before it keeps a module, it runs the same license and health gates as `enableAddon`.

After the first boot load, the browser re-reads the UI catalog and `addons/frontend-catalog` when an addon is reported disabled or unknown, when `AddonGuard` unloads a disabled addon, and when the tab regains focus. Those refreshes are capped at one full cycle per minute (no faster polling loop).

Tier 1 server modules load with a `contentHash` query on the entry `import()` URL when the manifest carries `contentHash`, so an approved update with a new hash loads new server code without a backend restart. Disable then enable the same installed folder reuses the cached module for that hash. Each distinct hash stays in the process until the API restarts, so restart the API after a long run of tier 1 updates. Tier 1 addon authors must not keep mutable state at module scope (top-level `let`, caches, or singletons); use `initialize()` / disposers or per-request state instead.

Disable does not abort tier 1 work that has already started. That request, queue job, or event handler finishes. A request that arrives after the route is removed is not handled. A job or event that has not started is not delivered. A tier 2 call still inside the child is rejected. Its HTTP route answers **503** with `tier 2 addon <id> stopped`. A job or event delivery in flight fails the same way, and a later one is not sent to the child.

## Split workers

`RUN_MODE=all` registers and removes an addon's job handlers in the same process as the toggle. `RUN_MODE=workers` does not share that memory. That process reads `addon_configurations.is_enabled` at job time and again every 15 seconds. A disabled addon's handlers are removed, and a job for it is refused and not retried. A newly enabled addon's handlers are registered on that pass, after the same load the process uses at startup. If the enabled set cannot be read, addon jobs are refused and retried, and the handlers stay as they are. Core jobs are not checked. A worker restart is not required for a toggle. The 15-second window is `ADDON_JOB_ENABLEMENT_CACHE_MS` in `server/workers/addonJobEnablement.ts`.

## Release steps and seeds

Day-0 and later SQL are listed in [release steps](../deployment/release-steps.md). Apply them with `npm run release:apply` on a database that already exists. A rebuild does not re-run init scripts.

Seeds and migrations this kit depends on:

| Script                                                            | Why                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `database/seeds/overlays/20261027_agent_autonomy.sql`             | `agents.autonomy.*` settings. An agent call fails closed when the threshold is missing.                                                                                                                 |
| Tier 2 settings in the day-0 schema                               | `addons.tier2.*` and the egress limits. A tier 2 child will not start without them.                                                                                                                     |
| `database/migrations/20261027_audit_logs_append_only.sql`         | Audit rows cannot be updated or deleted.                                                                                                                                                                |
| `database/migrations/20261028_addon_publisher_trust.sql`          | Publisher trust tables, the kassis key, and the approval policies for adding or rotating a key and for changing tiers or prefixes. The add-policy id is `…026`; `…021` is already `mcp_final_decision`. |
| `database/migrations/20261028_addon_publisher_key_add_policy.sql` | Existing databases that applied the first seed still need this row. Without it, key add returns 503.                                                                                                    |
| `database/migrations/20261028_addon_deployment_staged.sql`        | `DeploymentState.staged`, and the approval policies for an addon install and for a rollback that widens access.                                                                                         |
| `database/migrations/20261026_db_roles_audit_owner.sql`           | `kassis_app` and the audit owner.                                                                                                                                                                       |
| `database/migrations/20261116_addon_database_roles.sql`           | Per-addon migration role and run-time role for schema `addon_<id>`. Apply with the release ledger. Tier 2 install calls it.                                                                              |
| `database/migrations/20261116_addon_schema_migrations.sql`        | Ledger and apply function for tier 2 package up scripts. Apply after the roles step, before a backend that installs those packages.                                                                     |
| `database/migrations/20261116_addon_schema_migration_revert.sql`  | Revert function for tier 2 down scripts. Apply after the schema-migration step, before a backend that rolls those packages back.                                                                        |

**Prod empty volume.** Prod compose does not load the full schema on an empty volume. Only the roles script runs. Restore a backup or apply the release ledger. On-prem does load the day-0 schema, because that file is the new-site install. Details are in the release steps.

## On-prem and air-gapped

On-prem uses `docker-compose.onprem.yml`. Air-gapped install uses the bundle from [Install](./install.md). The bundle has the public verification key and does not have the private key.

## Troubleshooting

| What you see                                                         | What to do                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Addon page is blank and the console says `register` is missing       | Export `register` from `frontend/index.ts`.                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| `{"ok":false,"issues":[...]}` from `certify --json`                  | The `issues` array names the KADK codes. KADK-709 is a missing lock (`sync` first). KADK-701 is a missing attestation (`attest`, then fill the answers).                                                                                             |
| Tier 2 addon does not start                                          | Check `addons.tier2.*`, `addons.egress.*`, and `addons.capabilities.timeoutMs` in Settings, including `addons.tier2.stopTimeoutMs`. An invalid or missing value refuses the start. The same capability timeout bounds extension callbacks. Apply release step `20261116-tier2-capability-timeout` when the capability timeout is missing. |
| Tier 2 child still running after disable                             | Disable, update and uninstall signal the child through the host disposer and kill it if it has not exited within `addons.tier2.stopTimeoutMs`. Host shutdown waits for that stop.                                                                  |
| Revoked key still in `previous`                                      | Revoke it with `POST /api/v1/platform/addon-publishers/:id/keys/:fp/revoke`, or set status `revoked` in `KASSIS_PUBLISHER_TRUST_FILE`. A revoked row in either source wins. Listing it as `previous` does not keep it trusted.                       |
| Fresh prod database has roles and no tables                          | Expected. Restore or run `npm run release:apply`. Do not expect the prod compose file to create the schema.                                                                                                                                          |
| Agent tool returns an approval id instead of changing the case       | The tool is a final decision and the run is not attested, or autonomy is not `act`. Approve it in the Approvals UI.                                                                                                                                  |
| Bank addon does not load                                             | The publisher must be approved, the key must be `current` or `previous`, the addon id must start with one of that publisher's prefixes, and the tier must be 2. Tier 1 is only for kassis.                                                           |
| Upload returns 503                                                   | Apply `20261028-addon-deployment-staged` and publish an `addon_deployment` policy. A missing policy does not install the package. Key add 503 is the missing `addon_publisher_key` / `add` policy — apply `20261028-addon-publisher-key-add-policy`. |
| Backend crash: missing approval evidence module on startup           | Rebuild the backend image from a current kassis release. If you maintain the image Dockerfile, see [Maintainers](./maintainers.md).                                                                                                                     |
| MCP HTTP crash: `Cannot find module '/app/server/prisma.js'`         | The MCP image does not ship Prisma. Publisher trust then uses the seeded file. Rebuild MCP.                                                                                                                                                          |

## ADK catalog

`GET /api/v1/adk/catalog` needs a signed-in user with `system.admin`. `GET /api/v1/adk/version` stays open and still returns only `hostApi`.

The catalog is built from `@kassis/addon-sdk` tier-matrix data and the host registries. It lists facade method names with tier flags and the permission each call needs, capability ids with version and owning addon, event names with their JSON schemas, host slot, deep-link and source names, and reserved permission namespaces. It does not return capability implementations, settings values, tenant rows, or secrets.

## Process packs (kind 1)

Installing or updating a package that lists `process.packs[]` creates case templates, flow templates and lifecycle policies as drafts. The host calls the existing template and lifecycle services. A case template's `linked_flow_key` and `lifecycle_policy_key` are pack keys and are stored as the ids created for those packs. `source_addon`, `source_key` and `source_version` record the package. Drafts stay unpublished, and a lifecycle pack is not made the default. A listed kind other than those three stops the install. A `source_key` that is already present is left unchanged. Apply release step `20261116-process-pack-provenance` on a database that does not already have those columns.

## Tier 2 package migrations

Installing or updating a tier 2 package applies `migrations/*.up.sql` from that package. The host provisions schema `addon_<id>` (hyphens in the id become underscores), then runs each pending up script as role `addon_<id>_migrate` inside the install or update lease. The script and its checksum row commit together. A script that fails leaves that script unapplied; scripts that already committed stay applied, and the install or update stops. A script whose file changed after it was applied is refused. The same file name in two packages is two rows. The app role is not a member of the migration role.

Each script must be ordinary SQL that can run in one transaction. It cannot contain psql commands, its own `COMMIT`, or the text `$kassis_mig$`. One script has to finish within the server's interactive transaction timeout (`PRISMA_TX_TIMEOUT_MS`, 30 seconds by default). There is no schema dump before the run; a failed script rolls back with its ledger row. Down scripts are not run on install or update.

Rolling back a tier 2 package runs `migrations/*.down.sql` for each applied script the target version does not contain, newest name first, as `addon_<id>_migrate`. The down script and the deletion of its ledger row commit together. A script marked `irreversible: true` in its `<name>.json` marker blocks that rollback before any down script runs. The install approval shows those migration names and `automaticRollback: blocked`. Apply release step `20261116-addon-schema-migration-revert` before rolling a package back. Uninstall does not export or drop the schema.

Tier 1 packages are not migrated by this path.

## Uninstall retention

Uninstall reads `data.retention` on a v2 manifest (`retain`, `archive`, `purge`). When that field is absent it still reads v1 `database.dataRetentionPolicy` (`retain`, `archive`, `delete`). `retain` and `archive` leave prefixed tables in place. `delete` and `purge` report leftover prefixed tables as residuals. `purge` writes one `retention_purge` audit row. Exporting or dropping the addon schema is the migration runner, not this check.

## Package deploy

`POST /api/v1/addon-security/deploy` accepts `.addon` (zip) and `.tar.gz`. The upload temp file often has no extension; the host sniffs zip (`PK`) and gzip magic when the name is not `.addon`, `.zip`, or `.tar.gz`. It checks the signature and recomputes `contentHash` on the extracted folder before anything is copied. `manifest.checksum` is not compared. An optional `archiveSha256` field is compared to the uploaded bytes and protects the transfer only.

`GET /api/v1/platform/addons/installations` lists each addon id, the active version, the publisher, and pending staged versions. It uses the same `system.admin` token as deploy. It does not return secrets. `kassis-addon status` calls this route.

A valid package creates a `platform_addon_deployments` row in `staged` and an `addon_deployment` approval. On approval the host copies the package to `addons-installed/<id>/<version>/` and keeps older version folders. Tier 2 is then enabled through the lifecycle API, and the supervisor starts the child without a process restart. Enable of a manifest v2 addon refuses `MANDATORY_CONTRACT` (HTTP 409) when a record access check returns true or only throws, when a deletion handler is empty or only throws, when a declared record type has no access check, or when owned tables have no deletion handler. The same rules are KADK-729 to KADK-732 on `kassis-addon check` and `certify`. v1 addons are not part of that check. A tier 1 package from a publisher other than `kassis` is refused. A `kassis` tier 1 package is stored and is not hot-started; enable and disable stay on the lifecycle API.

The version must be higher than the installed one, and the addon id must match the manifest id pattern. An id already owned by another publisher is refused. `hostApi` must accept this instance's host API (`1.0.0`).

`POST /api/v1/platform/addons/:id/rollback` with `{ "targetVersion": "<version>" }` switches `active.json` back to a kept folder and is audited. It asks for approval only when that version adds permissions, egress hosts, or data access. `kassis-addon rollback` calls this route with the same `system.admin` token as `deploy` and `status`. The CLI refuses an addon id that is not a manifest id, a version that is not `x.y.z`, and an HTTP redirect. `addons-installed` is a volume on the compose stacks and a persistent volume claim in `deploy/k8s/production/deployment.yaml`. The loader looks in `addons/` first, then the active folder under `addons-installed`.

`kassis-addon dev` publishes the container on `127.0.0.1`. It also starts a pre-started tier 2 runner on an internal network (`kassis-tier2-<id>`) and points the backend at it. Neither container receives a Docker socket. The runner can reach the backend egress proxy and nothing else. Set `KASSIS_DEVHOST_ATTACH` to a running backend container name when that image needs the stack network and secrets. The dev process uses `RUN_MODE=api`, so it does not take the background jobs.

A production instance uses the same shape. Leave `KASSIS_TIER2_CONTAINER_RUNNERS` unset to keep the process runner (accident isolation). Set it to `host:port` pairs the orchestrator already started, one per addon, and set `KASSIS_TIER2_EGRESS_ADVERTISE_HOST` to the name those containers use for the API. Apply [tier2-runner-network-policy.yaml](../../../../deploy/k8s/production/tier2-runner-network-policy.yaml). The local overlay is `docker compose -f docker-compose.yml -f deploy/docker/docker-compose.tier2-runner.yml`. Do not mount `/var/run/docker.sock` or `/run/secrets` into the runner. The addon package directory must be visible at the same path in the runner as the path the backend sends.

MCP discovery lists a tier 2 tool from `contributions.mcp` on an active installed addon when that addon's signature still verifies. A revoked signing key removes the tool from the next discovery load. The MCP container image does not ship a database client, so that load on the MCP container still reads the trust file. The backend discovery load reads the database.

Enable and disable reach MCP without a process restart. List and call read `GET /api/v1/addons/status` and keep that result for `MCP_ADDON_STATUS_CACHE_MS` (five seconds when unset). A disabled addon's tools are left off the list, and a call returns `Addon <id> is disabled`. A newly enabled addon's tools are loaded on the next list or call after the cache expires, through the same signature and trust gate as startup. If that status read fails or the body is not a list, addon tools are withheld and a call returns `Addon <id> tools are unavailable because addon state could not be read`. Core tools stay listed. An addon that is not in the status list is still offered.

## Changelog

| Date       | Change                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 2026-11-19 | `kassis-addon rollback` refuses a non-manifest addon id, a non-`x.y.z` version, and an HTTP redirect. |
| 2026-11-19 | Documented `kassis-addon rollback` for `POST /api/v1/platform/addons/:id/rollback` (same `KASSIS_ADK_TOKEN` and `system.admin` gate as deploy and status). |
| 2026-11-19 | Live lab and backend image kit paths moved to [Maintainers](./maintainers.md).                                                                                                                          |
| 2026-11-16 | The live lab workflow runs `--only=H` after L1–L22. That step hot-toggles `acme-swift-approval` against `GET /api/v1/adk/version` and trusts the lab acme key only through `KASSIS_PUBLISHER_TRUST_FILE`. |
| 2026-11-16 | MCP status poll sends the first `CORS_ORIGIN` (default `http://localhost`) and `Authorization` when `KASSIS_MCP_STATUS_BEARER` is set. One addon whose MCP contribution fails to load is skipped; other tools stay listed. Lab secret files are mode 0644. A mode switch clears a leftover `KASSIS_PUBLISHER_TRUST_FILE`. |
| 2026-11-16 | Install and update also draft list, entity, dashboard and data-flow templates, policy, flag, QA and compliance rules, and questionnaire, prompt and email templates. They are not published. Apply `20261116-process-pack-provenance` first. Questionnaire packs also need `20261114-questionnaire-hardening`. |
| 2026-11-16 | Install and update create kind-1 process packs (case template, flow template, lifecycle policy) as drafts and set provenance. Apply `20261116-process-pack-provenance` first on a database that lacks the columns.                                                     |
| 2026-11-16 | Tier 2 container runner is opt-in via `KASSIS_TIER2_CONTAINER_RUNNERS`. `kassis-addon dev` starts that runner on an internal network. Apply `deploy/k8s/production/tier2-runner-network-policy.yaml` on the cluster.                                                  |
| 2026-11-16 | Disable lets in-flight tier 1 requests, jobs, and event handlers finish, and does not start new ones. An in-flight tier 2 call is rejected; the HTTP route answers 503 `tier 2 addon <id> stopped`.                                                                    |
| 2026-11-16 | Tier 2 rollback runs down scripts as `addon_<id>_migrate`. An irreversible migration blocks that rollback and is named on the install approval. Apply `20261116-addon-schema-migration-revert` first. |
| 2026-11-16 | Tier 2 install and update apply package up scripts as `addon_<id>_migrate`, one transaction per script with its checksum. Apply release step `20261116-addon-schema-migrations` first. Tier 1 is unchanged. Uninstall does not drop the schema. |
| 2026-11-16 | `GET /api/v1/adk/catalog` returns facade names, event schemas, capability ids, host slot names and reserved permission namespaces for `system.admin`. It does not return implementations or secrets.                                                                   |
| 2026-11-16 | Enable of a manifest v2 addon returns `MANDATORY_CONTRACT` when canAccess returns true or only throws, or onDelete is empty or only throws (KADK-729 to KADK-732). v1 addons are unchanged. |
| 2026-11-16 | Runtime-load UIs re-read `addons/ui-catalog` and `addons/frontend-catalog` on disable, unknown enablement, and tab focus (at most once per minute).                                                                                                                      |
| 2026-11-16 | Tier 1 `import()` is keyed by manifest `contentHash` so hot updates load new server code; disable then enable of the same hash reuses the module. Authors must avoid module-level mutable state.                                                                       |
| 2026-11-16 | Uninstall applies v2 `data.retention` (`retain`, `archive`, `purge`) and still accepts v1 `delete`. `purge` adds one `retention_purge` audit row. Prefixed tables left behind fail the residual check for `delete` and `purge`.                                        |
| 2026-11-16 | MCP list and call follow addon enablement from `GET /api/v1/addons/status`, cached for `MCP_ADDON_STATUS_CACHE_MS` (default five seconds). A failed read withholds addon tools. Core tools stay. A process restart is not required.                                      |
| 2026-11-16 | Release step `20261116-addon-database-roles` adds the per-addon migration and run-time database roles. Apply it with `npm run release:apply`.                                                                                                                          |
| 2026-11-16 | Tier 2 extension callbacks wait the same `addons.capabilities.timeoutMs`. A disabled, crashed, or slow addon fails closed. No new setting.                                                                                                                                |
| 2026-11-16 | Tier 2 capability calls wait `addons.capabilities.timeoutMs` (release step `20261116-tier2-capability-timeout`). A missing value refuses the child start.                                                                                                               |
| 2026-11-16 | Split workers follow addon enablement from `addon_configurations` within 15 seconds. A disabled addon's jobs are refused without retry. A worker restart is not required for a toggle.                                                                                 |
| 2026-11-14 | `KASSIS_DEVHOST_ATTACH` makes `kassis-addon dev` join that container's network and secrets and run as `RUN_MODE=api`.                                                                                                                                                    |
| 2026-11-14 | Installed tier 2 MCP tools are listed only while the signing key still verifies. A revoked key drops the tool on the next discovery load.                                                                                                                              |
| 2026-11-14 | Disable, update and uninstall stop a tier 2 child. The wait before the process is killed is `addons.tier2.stopTimeoutMs` (release step `20261114-tier2-stop-timeout`). Host shutdown waits for the same stop.                                                          |
| 2026-11-03 | Runtime addon CSS loads again. `/runtime-addons.json` entries are `{ js, css }`, the ui-catalog lists `styleFiles`, and the loader links them before the import. Addon settings pages had rendered without their stylesheets since the 2026-10-27 runtime-load change. |
| 2026-10-28 | The `addon_publisher_key` add policy uses id `…026` so it does not collide with `mcp_final_decision`. Existing databases apply `20261028-addon-publisher-key-add-policy`. Deploy sniffs zip/gzip magic when the upload temp file has no extension.                     |
| 2026-10-28 | The production backend image ships approval evidence helpers so host approval evidence can load after the server tree is flattened onto `/app`. MCP HTTP falls back to the seeded publisher-trust file when Prisma is not in the image.                                 |
| 2026-10-28 | `GET /api/v1/platform/addons/installations` returns the active version, publisher, and pending staged versions for each addon id.                                                                                                                                      |
| 2026-10-28 | Package upload stages an `addon_deployment` approval and installs to `addons-installed/<id>/<version>/`. Tier 2 enables without a restart. Rollback is `POST /api/v1/platform/addons/:id/rollback`.                                                                    |
| 2026-10-28 | Runtime UI requests include `contentHash`. The host serves `/addons-ui/<id>/*` only after the signature gate, while the addon is enabled and the content-hash and UI-hash fingerprints still match. First-party publishers do not need `uiContentHash`.                |
| 2026-10-28 | Apply `20261028_addon_publisher_trust` before a bank signing key can be stored. Revocation is immediate.                                                                                                                                                               |

# Publishing

**Status:** GA
**Version checked:** 2026-10-28
**Technical owner:** Platform Engineering (ADK)
**Last reviewed:** 2026-11-19

Version rules are in the [semver policy](../addons/semver-policy.md). Do not bump a public export of `@kassis/addon-sdk` without a matching report change.

## npm registry (kit packages)

`@kassis/addon-sdk`, `@kassis/adk-core`, `@kassis/mcp-contract`, `@kassis/addon-cli`, and `@kassis/addon-testkit` share kit version `0.1.0`. `@kassis/addon-ui`, `@kassis/host-sdk`, and `@kassis/agent-kit` publish on their own lines and are also `0.1.0` today. All of them publish publicly to npmjs.com under the `@kassis` scope, with npm provenance once the source repository is public. `manifest.hostApi` stays `^1.0.0`. Workspace layout, API Extractor reports, changesets, and air-gap bundling are described in [Maintainers](./maintainers.md) for people working in the kassis repository. The `@kassis/adk-core` tarball ships compiled JavaScript. Use `@kassis/addon-cli` for commands.

## Addon package

`kassis-addon package` writes `<id>-<version>.addon` beside the addon folder. The file is a zip. It contains the signed `manifest.json`, the files covered by `contentHash`, the certify evidence pack (`checks.json`, `attestation.json`, and `agent-profile.lock.json`), and `sbom.json`. `kassis-addon sbom` writes that SBOM from the addon build and `package-lock.json`. `package` writes it when it is missing or older than the server build. `package` does not sign the manifest and does not call the network. It refuses a manifest that has no signature or no `contentHash`, a folder whose certify evidence does not match `contentHash`, and a folder whose certify checks did not all exit 0. `sbom.json` is inside the content hash, so run `sign` after it changes and before `package`. `frontend/dist` stays outside the hash. When that folder exists, `package` still copies it into the zip so the host can serve `/addons-ui/<id>/`. A later image rebuild of first-party UI does not change `contentHash`.

`kassis-addon deploy --instance=<url>` uploads that file to `POST /api/v1/addon-security/deploy` and prints the approval request id. The token is `KASSIS_ADK_TOKEN`. An optional `archiveSha256` field is the sha256 of the uploaded bytes and checks the transfer only. The same command works from a jump host that has the `.addon` file. `kassis-addon status --instance=<url>` calls `GET /api/v1/platform/addons/installations` and prints the installed version and the pending staged versions. That route uses the same admin token as deploy. The body is the addon id, the active version, the publisher, and the pending versions. It does not include secrets.

## Instance install

The host does not compare `manifest.checksum` to the archive. The manifest is inside the package, so that digest cannot be a property of the package. Integrity is the signature plus `contentHash`, recomputed on the extracted folder before the host copies anything. An optional upload field `archiveSha256` is compared to the uploaded bytes and protects the transfer only.

The install path is `addons-installed/<id>/<version>/`. The version must be higher than the one already installed. A lower version is a rollback, not an install. `hostApi` must accept the instance host API. A tier 1 package is refused unless the publisher is `kassis`. Install waits for an `addon_deployment` approval. See [Operators](./operators.md).

## Changelog

| Date       | Change                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |

# Quickstart

**Status:** GA
**Version checked:** 2026-10-28
**Technical owner:** Platform Engineering (ADK)
**Last reviewed:** 2026-11-19

These steps were run in a folder outside any kassis checkout. Replace `<scratch>` with an empty directory. Install the CLI first ([Install](./install.md)).

## Create

```bash
npx kassis-addon init --id=sample-tprm-check --publisher=kassis --dir=<scratch>
```

Exit 0. `<scratch>/manifest.json` exists. `--publisher` defaults to `kassis`. `--tier` defaults to 2. Publisher `kassis` may pass `--tier=1`. Any other publisher is tier 2, and `--tier=1` exits 1. `--rung` defaults to 1.

| Rung | What init writes                               |
| ---- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| 1    | Server only. No `src/ui` and no `migrations/`. |
| 2    | Server and UI. No `migrations/`.               |
| 3    | Server, UI, and `migrations/`.                 |

A publisher other than `kassis` gets an id prefix. `--publisher=acme --id=widget` writes id `acme-widget`. An id that already starts with `acme-` is kept. `kassis` keeps the id you pass. `hostApi` is `^1.0.0`. `entrypoints.main` is `dist/server/index.js`. `signing` is omitted until `sign`. When the rung has a UI, `ui.entryFile` is `index.js`, relative to `frontend/dist`.

## Build and test

From `<scratch>`, after init:

```bash
npm install
npm run build
npm test
```

`npm run build` prints `dist/server/index.js`. It exits 1 when that file does not export `initialize`. For rung 2 or 3 it also prints `frontend/dist/index.js` and exits 1 when that file does not export `register`. The server bundle is ESM and leaves `@kassis/*` external. The UI bundle leaves the modules in `@kassis/addon-sdk/browser-externals.json` external.

`npm test` runs `test/server.test.ts`. That test calls `createTestContext()` and does not need a database. `build:server` and `build:ui` build one output. `check` and `certify` run the CLI commands below.

## Check and conformance

From `<scratch>`:

```bash
npx kassis-addon check
npx kassis-addon conformance
```

Both exit 0 and print nothing when the template is valid. `check --json` prints `{ "ok", "issues", "data" }`. A schema failure includes a KADK-1xx code.

## Profile, certify, pack

```bash
npx kassis-addon sync --profile=addon-coding-agent
```

Prints the path of `.kassis/agent-profile.lock.json` and writes `AGENTS.md` plus the rule files. Then write `.kassis/attestation.json` with one `followed` answer per guardrail in the lock (machine checks set `evidence.checkId`).

```bash
npx kassis-addon certify --json
```

Expected when the attestation matches the lock:

```json
{ "ok": true, "issues": [] }
```

Exit 0. A failing certify still prints JSON and exits 1.

```bash
npx kassis-addon pack --out=evidence
```

Prints `evidence` and exits 0.

## Dev and test

`dev` starts a container only when a dev host image is already configured and already present locally. Set `KASSIS_DEVHOST_IMAGE`, pass `--image`, or write `{ "image": "<name>" }` to `~/.kassis/devhost.json`. The command uses Docker or Podman. It does not build an image and does not pull one unless the CLI resolves a published default image tag. The addon directory is mounted read-only at `/opt/kassis/dev-addon`. It also starts a tier 2 runner container on an internal network and does not mount a Docker socket into the backend. It prints a `http://127.0.0.1` URL and follows the container logs. If the runtime or the image is missing, it exits 1 with an issue.

`migrate up`, `migrate down`, `migrate status` and `migrate claim` run only against that dev host database. With no dev host, they exit 1.

History is kept per addon id from `manifest.json`, so two addons can both ship `001_init.up.sql`. Each script runs in one transaction together with its history row: a failing script leaves no schema change and no row, and `up` can simply run again. Runs for the same addon wait for each other. A script edited after it was applied stops `up` and `down`; restore it or add a new migration. A script may contain its own `BEGIN;` … `COMMIT;`, but not statements that cannot run in a transaction (`CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`, `VACUUM`).

A dev host database used with an older ADK has history rows without an addon id. `status` lists them as `unclaimed`, and `up` stops on them because they could belong to another addon. In the addon that owns them, run `migrate claim`.

```bash
npx kassis-addon dev
npx kassis-addon test
```

Use `npm test` for the template. The CLI `test` command runs `node --test` in `./test`. It prints `No test directory` and exits 0 when that folder is missing.

## Sign

`sign` without `--key` uses the host signer only when the CLI is wired to one (first-party publish flows). Outside that setup, `sign` without `--key` exits 1. `sign --key=<path>` writes `contentHash` and signs with that publisher key file. Do not commit the private key.

## Changelog

| Date       | Change                                                                                                                                                                               |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| 2026-11-19 | The template `.npmrc` pins `@kassis` to `https://registry.npmjs.org/` with no token. The certify workflow no longer needs a packages secret.                                          |
| 2026-11-19 | Quickstart uses `npx kassis-addon` only; repository entry points moved to [Maintainers](./maintainers.md).                                                                             |
| 2026-11-16 | `dev` starts a tier 2 runner container on an internal network. The backend container does not receive a Docker socket.                                                                |
| 2026-11-11 | `migrate` keeps history per addon, applies each script with its history row in one transaction, detects edited scripts, and adds `claim` (F024, F025).                               |
| 2026-10-28 | The template `.npmrc` points `@kassis` at GitHub Packages and reads `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`. The certify workflow uses Node 24 and that secret.                                            |
| 2026-10-28 | `dev` starts a configured local image and does not pull or build. `migrate` targets that dev host only. `check --json` includes KADK codes. `--id value` and `--id=value` both work. |
| 2026-10-28 | `init` accepts `--publisher`, `--tier`, and `--rung`. `npm run build` writes `dist/server/index.js` and, for a rung with UI, `frontend/dist/index.js`.                               |

# Signing and trust

**Status:** GA
**Version checked:** 2026-10-28
**Technical owner:** Platform Engineering (ADK)
**Last reviewed:** 2026-11-19

## Publisher keys

The instance trust store is the database (`platform_addon_publishers` and `platform_addon_publisher_keys`), merged with `server/core/addon-platform/trust/publisher-trust.json`. That file seeds publisher `kassis` so boot and unit tests can verify first-party addons before the database is up.

`KASSIS_PUBLISHER_TRUST_FILE`, when set, is a read-only JSON file in the same shape: `publishers` and `keys`, with key status `pending`, `current`, `previous`, or `revoked`. It is merged with the seeded file and the database. A `revoked` key in any source is revoked. A `suspended` publisher in any source is suspended.

`kassis` may sign tiers 1 and 2, and its id prefix `*` matches any addon id. A bank publisher is limited to tier 2. Each of its id prefixes must start with the publisher id and a hyphen, so publisher `acme` can sign `acme-tprm` and cannot sign `ubo-panel`. Tier 1 is refused for every publisher other than `kassis`. A key, a rotation, or a tier or prefix change stays pending until a second person approves it. If no approval policy is published, that change is refused.

`signing.keyId` on the manifest is the sha256 hex of the Ed25519 SPKI DER. The verifier loads that key. A bank key cannot sign `publisher: "kassis"`. A manifest with no `signing` block is verified only with the kassis current key, and only when `publisher` is `kassis` or the legacy first-party id `kassis-corp`. Any other publisher without `signing` is refused. `ADDON_VERIFICATION_PUBLIC_KEY` is only a bootstrap fallback for the kassis public key bytes.

Guardrail profiles still accept the kassis key, including a fingerprint listed as `previous` during rotation.

## Rotation and revocation

`current` and `previous` keys verify. `pending` does not, until an approver accepts it. Add the new key and wait for approval before you stop signing with the old one; approval moves the new key to `current` and the old one to `previous`.

Revocation is immediate and does not wait for approval. A revoked fingerprint is refused when signature checks are strict and when they are not. An invalid signature that is not a trust failure still warns and continues in non-strict mode, and only for `kassis` and `kassis-corp`. Any other named publisher is verified in strict mode whatever `ENABLE_STRICT_ADDON_SIGNATURES` says.

Addon load, deploy verification, and the MCP contribution loader call the same trust loader. A revocation emits `system.addon.publisher_trust.invalidated`. The in-process cache also expires after a short TTL, which covers a process that misses the event.

## Addon SBOM

`kassis-addon sbom` writes a CycloneDX document for the libraries this addon ships. `package` includes `sbom.json` in the `.addon` zip and in the content hash scope.

Signing npm kit tarballs is documented in [Maintainers](./maintainers.md).

## Content hash and runtime UI

`contentHash` covers the addon files in the kit content-hash scope. `frontend/dist/**` is outside that hash. A client publisher (not first-party: `kassis`, `kassis-corp`, or empty) with a `ui` block also signs `uiContentHash` over `frontend/dist/**`. The host refuses the package when that field is missing or no longer matches, and does not serve the UI. First-party addons build that folder in the server image after the manifest is signed, so they do not carry `uiContentHash`. `frontend/src/**`, `frontend/node_modules/**`, `.kassis/**`, `.cursor/**`, `.claude/**`, `.github/**`, `evidence/**` and `test/**` are outside the hash too. A scope change changes every hash. Re-sign with `npm run sign:addons`.

`GET /addons-ui/<id>/*` is served only when that addon passed the signature gate on its last load and is enabled. Each response re-checks the content-hash and UI-hash cache fingerprints (file size, mtime and ctime) and does not re-read file bytes when those fingerprints still match. Any other case is 404.

Loading an addon runs this gate before the host registers anything for it, so a package refused for its signature or `contentHash` leaves no frontend, table-prefix or license-feature entry. Install and update run the same gate on the staged copy before it is promoted or committed ([Managing addons](../addons/managing-addons.md#install-and-update-one-folder-per-attempt)).

The runtime UI catalog entry carries `contentHash`. The loader appends it as a query string (`?contentHash=`), so a browser cache does not mix versions.

## Changelog

| Date       | Change                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 2026-11-19 | Content-hash scope is the kit scope. The file path lives on [Maintainers](./maintainers.md).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| 2026-11-19 | Client docs use `kassis-addon sbom`; kit tarball signing moved to [Maintainers](./maintainers.md).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| 2026-11-11 | The signature and `contentHash` gate runs before any host registration when an addon loads; a failed load disposes the addon's registrations. Install and update run the same gate on the staged package before promotion.                                                                                                          |
| 2026-10-28 | First-party publishers (`kassis`, `kassis-corp`, empty) do not need `uiContentHash`. A client UI package signs it over `frontend/dist`. A missing or mismatched client hash is refused, and the UI route returns 404. The UI gate reuses a stat fingerprint cache.                                                                  |
| 2026-10-28 | Tool, evidence, test, and `frontend/dist/**` folders are outside `contentHash`. The server image builds `frontend/dist` after signing. Runtime UI is served only after a passing signature gate while the addon stays enabled and the content-hash fingerprint still matches. The catalog `contentHash` is the loader query string. |
| 2026-10-28 | Trust is the database plus the seeded file and optional `KASSIS_PUBLISHER_TRUST_FILE`. Revoked wins. Bank publishers are always strict, cannot use tier 1, and their id prefixes must start with the publisher id and a hyphen. A key or scope change is refused when no approval policy is published.                              |

# Testing

**Status:** GA
**Version checked:** 2026-10-28
**Technical owner:** Platform Engineering (ADK)
**Last reviewed:** 2026-11-19

`@kassis/addon-testkit` checks an evidence pack. `checkAddonImports` is the import boundary used by `assertNoHostImports` and by the CLI `conformance` command.

`createTestContext()` reads `manifest.json` from the current working directory when you do not pass `manifest` or `manifestPath`. It maps the manifest onto the same declared-name lists the host uses and refuses undeclared `audit`, `events`, `jobs`, `prompts`, `secrets` and `egress` calls with the same KADK codes (606, 401, 610, 608, 605, 607). Pass `tier: 1` or `tier: 2` (default `2`). For that tier, `capabilities`, `locks`, `extend`, and `data` fakes consult `@kassis/addon-sdk/tier-matrix.json` and throw KADK-219 when the manifest tier cannot use the facade, matching `kassis-addon doctor --requirements`. Tier 2 may call `capabilities.provide`, the wave 1 `extend` methods (`registerAuditSubject`, `registerDeletable`, `registerDocumentable`, `registerLinkable`, `registerRecordAccess`), the wave 2 methods (`registerApprovable`, `registerApprovableFields`, `registerCommunicable`), the wave 3 method (`registerFlaggable`), the wave 4 automation methods (`registerAutomationTrigger`, `registerAutomationAction`, `registerAutomationFields`), the wave 5 methods (`registerRiskFactors`, `registerAnalyticsContributor`, `registerGraphRiskMirror`, `registerPredictionCapability`), and the wave 6 methods (`registerInvestigationDomain`, `registerInvestigationTemplate`, `registerEchoStrategy`, `registerQuestionnaireDomain`, `setQuestionnaireDomainAdapter`, `importQuestionnairePack`, `registerEmployeeDirectory`). `capabilities.register`, `registerLicenseFeatures`, `registerShutdownHook`, `locks`, and Prisma data helpers stay refused. Tier 2 `data.query` / `execute` / `transaction` are allowed. Wave 1 through wave 6 extend calls are recorded on `ctx.recorded.extend`. Pass an explicit manifest in unit tests when the working directory is not the addon root.

Every top-level `AddonContext` member has an in-memory fake: `config`, `routes` (including `principalOf`), `data`, `core` (cases, approvals, parties, entities, documents, users), `risk`, `settings`, `flags`, `notify`, `prompts`, plus the earlier audit/events/jobs/llm/http/secrets/capabilities/locks/extend recorders. Calls land on `ctx.recorded.*`. A unit test walks `keyof AddonContext` and fails when a new SDK member has no testkit entry.

JavaScript is read with `es-module-lexer` (static `import`, dynamic `import()`, and `export ... from`). `require()` is not an ECMAScript import, so the TypeScript scanner records it. `.ts` files use that scanner for every form.

An import is allowed when the specifier is a relative path that stays inside the addon folder, one of `@kassis/addon-sdk`, `@kassis/host-sdk`, `@kassis/addon-ui`, or `@kassis/agent-kit`, a package named in `dependencies`, `optionalDependencies`, or `peerDependencies`, or a Node built-in in server code. Server code is every checked file except `src/ui/` and `frontend/`. Anything else fails with a KADK-2xx code, the file, and the line: KADK-201 for the host alias `@/`, KADK-202 for Kassis core (`server/`), KADK-203 for the core capability registry, KADK-204 for a relative path outside the package, and KADK-205 for an undeclared package or a Node built-in in UI code.

`conformance` runs that check on `src/`, `frontend/`, and, when the files exist, `dist/server/index.js` and `frontend/dist/index.js`. A migration that goes up still needs a down script.

`certify` runs the CLI commands `check`, `conformance`, `build` and `test`, then `requirements`, `plan`, and the pinned-profile attestation check, then computes the content hash. It writes `.kassis/evidence/checks.json` with the CLI version, the Node version, and for each check the input hash, exit code, duration and output digest. `adk.attest-pinned-profile` exits 0 when no profile is pinned. When a lock is present it exits 0 only if `.kassis/attestation.json` matches that lock and answers every guardrail.

An outcome must be `followed`, `violated` or `not_applicable`. Anything else, including a blank string or null, fails with KADK-714. The helper that prepares a new attestation writes null for each outcome so the file fails until it is answered.

Machine evidence comes only from `.kassis/evidence/checks.json`. Evidence typed into the attestation is ignored and reported as KADK-715. That warning does not fail certify. A followed machine guardrail with no passing row for its check fails with KADK-707.

`certify` fails on KADK-701 through KADK-711 and on KADK-714. Advisory KADK-712, KADK-713 and KADK-715 do not fail it. Codes are listed in [KADK error codes](../reference/adk-error-codes.md).

The KADK checks that matter while you are writing an addon:

- the manifest matches v2 (`check`)
- imports stay inside the addon boundary (`conformance`)
- a migration that goes up can come down (`conformance`)
- the attestation matches the signed profile lock (`certify`)

Tier 2 isolation is covered by `n14Tier2Isolation` (no host database URL in the child, egress refusal, and disable after the restart limit). Those tests load the `sample-tprm-check` fixture. They do not install it into the product addon list.

Pack only after certify passes. It writes `index.json` and `README.md` in the output directory, plus the attestation, the lock and the certify result. `index.json` holds:

- the change summary from `.kassis/change-summary.json` (`reference`, `rung`, `why`, `summary`), including the rung and why
- the manifest diff against `.kassis/previous-manifest.json` (permissions, egress hosts, events, capabilities, data access and tier; when that file is missing, every current value is listed as added)
- migrations, with up and down status (`present`, `missing`, `irreversible` or `unknown`)
- the test and conformance rows from the checks file
- the SBOM of the addon `package.json` dependencies
- the content hash, the signer fingerprint (`signing.keyId`) and the CLI version

```bash
npx kassis-addon pack --out=evidence
```

Repository CI builds the reference addon `acme-swift-approval` and runs the hot-toggle live lab. See [Maintainers](./maintainers.md).

The tier 2 route bridge forwards the method, path, query, JSON body, and the caller principal. `GET /release-policy` remains a probe that does not need a body. A configuration save pushes the operator document into a running child (`config.replace`). When the manifest sets `health.path` and the addon mounted that route, a 5xx from the route marks the child unhealthy.

## Changelog

| Date       | Change                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 2026-11-19 | Reference-addon and live-lab detail moved to [Maintainers](./maintainers.md). Pack uses `npx kassis-addon`.                                                                                                      |
| 2026-11-16 | Live lab hot-toggle runs under a core request loop. The acme key is trusted only through the lab trust file. |
| 2026-11-16 | Reference addon `acme-swift-approval` is certified twice in repository CI. Live deploy stays outside that script. |
| 2026-11-16 | `createTestContext` allows tier 2 wave 6 `extend` methods and records them. License and shutdown extend methods, locks, `capabilities.register`, and Prisma data helpers still throw KADK-219. |
| 2026-11-16 | `createTestContext` fakes every `AddonContext` area (core.*, risk, settings, flags, notify, prompts, config, routes.principalOf) with recorders; SDK key walk fails when a member has no fake. |
| 2026-11-16 | Certify records `adk.requirement-plan-mapped` and `adk.attest-pinned-profile` in `checks.json` beside requirements tracing. |
| 2026-11-16 | `createTestContext` allows tier 2 wave 4 automation `extend` methods and records them. Later-wave extend methods still throw KADK-219. |
| 2026-11-16 | `createTestContext` allows tier 2 wave 2 `extend` methods (`registerApprovable`, `registerApprovableFields`, `registerCommunicable`) and records them. Later-wave extend methods still throw KADK-219. |
| 2026-11-16 | `createTestContext` allows tier 2 wave 1 `extend` methods and records them. Later-wave extend methods, locks, `capabilities.register`, and Prisma data helpers still throw KADK-219. |
| 2026-11-16 | `createTestContext` allows tier 2 `capabilities.provide` and still refuses extend, locks, `capabilities.register`, and data writes with KADK-219 from `tier-matrix.json`.                                          |
| 2026-11-16 | `createTestContext` enforces manifest declared-name lists for audit, events, jobs, prompts, secrets and egress with host KADK codes.                                                                          |
| 2026-10-28 | Conformance uses one import checker. Forbidden imports fail with KADK-201 through KADK-205, including `dist/server/index.js` and `frontend/dist/index.js` when those files exist.                             |
| 2026-10-28 | Certify records check, conformance, build and test in `.kassis/evidence/checks.json`. A blank outcome is KADK-714. Typed machine evidence is KADK-715. The evidence pack writes `index.json` and `README.md`. |

documents.text:
# Tiers

Tier 2 process isolation is accident isolation until the container runner is the production default. The process runner starts the child under the Node permission model so it cannot read host files outside its package and the modules it must load, and it cannot spawn a process, a worker, or a native addon. The image user `kassis-addon` is used only when the supervisor is root. On Node 24.18.1 there is no network permission flag, so the child can still open its own TCP socket, including to Postgres.

**Status:** GA
**Version checked:** 2026-10-28
**Technical owner:** Platform Engineering (ADK)
**Last reviewed:** 2026-11-16

## Tier 1

A tier 1 addon is loaded in the host process. `initialize()` runs there. This is the right tier for the first-party addons that ship with Kassis.

## Tier 2

Set `"tier": 2` on the manifest. The host does not import the addon. `superviseTier2Addon()` starts a `Tier2Runner`. The process runner (`createProcessTier2Runner`) is the implementation that spawns one child under `--permission` (read paths only; no `--allow-child-process`, `--allow-worker`, or `--allow-addons`). The child environment is the declared values plus the egress proxy, not the host `process.env`, so `DATABASE_URL` is absent. The runner's `start`, `stop`, `call`, and `health` are the only process controls the supervisor uses. A direct TCP socket is still possible: Node 24.18.1 rejects `--allow-net`.

The process runner is the default. That default is accident isolation: the addon is a child process on the host, not a separate container. The container runner is the production isolation target. Set `KASSIS_TIER2_CONTAINER_RUNNERS` to a comma-separated `host:port` list of pre-started generic runner containers. The backend dials that TCP port. It does not receive a Docker socket and it does not start containers. Each container loads and drops one addon package. The same JSON-RPC is used, including `capability.invoke`. The egress proxy is published to those containers at `KASSIS_TIER2_EGRESS_ADVERTISE_HOST` on `KASSIS_TIER2_EGRESS_PORT` (7401). The required network policy is [tier2-runner-network-policy.yaml](../../../../deploy/k8s/production/tier2-runner-network-policy.yaml): ingress only from the API pods to RPC port 7400, egress only to the API pods on the proxy port. A local compose overlay with the same limits is [docker-compose.tier2-runner.yml](../../../../deploy/docker/docker-compose.tier2-runner.yml). `kassis-addon dev` starts one runner on an internal network and does not mount a Docker socket into either container.

The child speaks JSON-RPC. The host mounts HTTP at `/api/v1/addons/<id>` and `POST /_mcp/:tool`. MCP discovery synthesizes tools that call those URLs. A caller must be a host-issued principal who holds every gate permission, or `system.admin` when the manifest declares none.

The supervisor enforces:

- egress hosts from the manifest (`egress.hosts`)
- a heap cap from `resources.memoryMb`
- restart and health limits from Settings

When the restart limit or the health-failure limit is hit, the supervisor disables the addon in the registry. The host process keeps running.

## Facade bridge

The child does not import core and does not receive `DATABASE_URL` or the host environment. `initialize(ctx)` runs in the child. Calls shaped `ctx.<facade>.<method>` go over the same JSON-RPC line to the facade objects `createAddonContext` builds for tier 1. The manifest policy and `AddonAccessGuard` are unchanged. The host inserts the addon's service principal. The child cannot choose that principal or a schema or role name.

The host provisions one IAM user per addon, `addon.<id>@service.kassis.local`, with role `addon_service`. That role has no grants until an operator adds them. A call the account cannot make is refused (KADK-615). A route permission that is not in the manifest is refused (KADK-216). The child cannot call `ctx.core.approvals.applyRegistered`. That call would let it choose `decidedBy`. The host delivers `approval.apply` when the engine approves a record type the addon owns.

`ctx.events.subscribe`, `ctx.jobs.register`, and `ctx.jobs.schedule` are registered on the host during `initialize()`. The host delivers them with `event.deliver` and `job.run`. A failed event delivery is written to the existing domain-events queue and retried there. A failed job stays on the job queue that `ctx.jobs` already uses. A child crash does not drop that work.

`ctx.capabilities.provide` is allowed when the capability id is in the addon namespace (`<id>.` or the id with hyphens turned into underscores) and that id and version are listed in `provides`. The implementation stays in the child. A consumer's call is forwarded to that process. The wait is Settings `addons.capabilities.timeoutMs`. If the provider is disabled, crashed, or does not answer in time, the consumer gets `null`. `ctx.capabilities.register` stays refused.

`ctx.extend.*` is accepted only for a point named in manifest `extends`. The host calls the child back with `extend.callback`, the acting principal, and the same Settings timeout as a capability call (`addons.capabilities.timeoutMs`). A disabled, crashed, or slow addon fails closed: an access check is not an allow, an approval stays pending, a deletion is retried, and an automation step errors. Wave 1 points on the allow-list are `registerAuditSubject`, `registerRecordAccess`, `registerDeletable`, `registerDocumentable`, and `registerLinkable`. Wave 2 adds `registerApprovable`, `registerApprovableFields`, and `registerCommunicable`. Wave 3 adds `registerFlaggable`. Wave 4 adds `registerAutomationTrigger`, `registerAutomationAction`, and `registerAutomationFields`. Wave 5 adds `registerRiskFactors`, `registerAnalyticsContributor`, `registerGraphRiskMirror`, and `registerPredictionCapability`. Wave 6 adds `registerInvestigationDomain`, `registerInvestigationTemplate`, `registerEchoStrategy`, `registerQuestionnaireDomain`, `setQuestionnaireDomainAdapter`, `importQuestionnairePack`, and `registerEmployeeDirectory`. Echo `compare` stays synchronous and returns no diff when the child cannot be called, so a refresh is not accepted on silence. `importQuestionnairePack` still reuses a live pack with the same domain and kind; disable retires a pack that call created and leaves a reused pack in place. A risk factor value is left out when the child is down. An analytics pull, a graph risk mirror, and a prediction throw, so a timeout does not become an empty or zero score. `communicable` is a manifest extend id. The host admits automation on the Flag Automation catalog, and a trigger or action callback errors when the addon is down. Those registrations are removed on disable. Two addons cannot own the same name (KADK-223). `onApproved` and `onRejected` call the child with the deciding user and stay pending when the child is down. `registerCommunicable` stores the owner type `ctx.core.communication.send` and `list` require. `registerFlaggable` calls `findUnique` and `findMany` on the child and throws when the child is down so the flag layer does not invent or drop flags. `ctx.notify.registerType` is limited to the addon namespace and is removed on disable. `ctx.extend.registerLicenseFeatures` and `ctx.extend.registerShutdownHook` stay refused for tier 2 (decision D-S227 in the ADK consolidated plan). A shutdown hook is awaited with no timeout inside host shutdown, so a client handler could hold the process. License registration writes a process-wide catalog that replaces the platform keys `core`, `analytics`, `automation` and `integrations` and the same key from another addon, and `defaultAccess: true` is treated as allowed when the signed license does not name the key. It does not return the tenant's license. Still refused in tier 2: `capabilities.register`, `locks`, and the Prisma helpers `ctx.data.$queryRaw`, `ctx.data.$executeRaw` and `ctx.data.$transaction`. `ctx.data.read` accepts a table name. The host qualifies it with `data.schema` (or `addon_<id>` when the manifest omits the schema) and reads only `database.ownedTables`. Any other table, or a name that contains a schema, is refused.

`ctx.data.query`, `ctx.data.execute` and `ctx.data.transaction` send one parameterised statement, or a batch of them. Placeholders are `$1`, `$2`, and so on. The host binds the JSON values. The statement runs as `addon_<id>_runtime` (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE on that schema only). The database function refuses a second command in the same string. The child does not name the role or the schema. On the first call the host installs `kassis_data_statement` in the add-on schema; that needs `kassis_provision_addon_database` (S2.01) to have created the schema. Statement timeout is Settings `addons.data.statementTimeoutMs` (seed 5000). A query that would return more rows than Settings `addons.data.rowCap` (seed 100) is refused. Both limits are read on the call. `ctx.data.read` uses the same row cap. A batch runs in one transaction and rolls back if any statement fails. Structure changes stay on the migration role. Every `execute` in `ctx.data.execute` or `ctx.data.transaction` gets a host baseline row in `audit_logs` (`ADDON_DATA_WRITE`: add-on id, parsed table, operation, row count). A write from a tier 2 HTTP route records the forwarded caller; jobs and events keep the addon service principal. The child cannot turn that off.

An MCP tool from `contributions.mcp` runs in the child. The server entry exports `tools`, a map from tool name to `handler(args, ctx)`. The child passes the same `ctx` that `initialize` received, or `null` when a call arrives before `initialize`. An addon does not keep `ctx` in module state (KADK-728).

The tier 2 RPC allow-list is `TIER2_FACADE_METHODS` in `server/core/addon-platform/tier2/tier2RpcAllowlist.ts`. The same list, plus every other `ctx` facade method and its tier 1 availability, ships as `@kassis/addon-sdk/tier-matrix.json`. `npm run ci:adk:tier-matrix` fails when that file disagrees with the allow-list. Business meaning: [Addons overview](../../business/addons/overview.md).

`sample-tprm-check` is the fixture the tier 2 tests load. It is not a product addon. On a local backend, installing a signed copy started the child with no `DATABASE_URL`. `GET /api/v1/addons/sample-tprm-check/health` returned 204. `POST /_mcp/probe.env` returned the child pid. Killing the child restarted it. Further kills left that route at 503, and the rest of the API still answered. The fixture was removed afterwards. A tier 2 addon does not need its own entry file.

## Settings

These keys are read from Settings. A missing or invalid value refuses to start the child. The two `addons.data` keys are read on each data call and refuse that call instead.

| Key                               | Meaning                               |
| --------------------------------- | ------------------------------------- |
| `addons.tier2.restartBackoffMs`   | Delay before a restart                |
| `addons.tier2.maxRestarts`        | Restarts before the addon is disabled |
| `addons.tier2.healthIntervalMs`   | Time between health probes            |
| `addons.tier2.healthFailureLimit` | Consecutive failures before disable   |
| `addons.egress.timeoutMs`         | Fetch timeout                         |
| `addons.egress.maxResponseBytes`  | Fetch response cap                    |
| `addons.capabilities.timeoutMs`   | Capability call and extension callback timeout |
| `addons.data.statementTimeoutMs`  | Timeout for one `ctx.data` statement  |
| `addons.data.rowCap`              | Most rows one `ctx.data` query may return |

## Changelog

| Date       | Change                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 2026-11-19 | A tier 2 MCP tool handler receives `(args, ctx)`. `acme-swift-approval` no longer keeps `ctx` in module state. |
| 2026-11-16 | Wave 6 opens investigation domain and template, echo strategy, questionnaire domain, adapter and pack import, and the employee directory for tier 2. Pack import retires only a pack that call created (S2.26). |
| 2026-11-16 | Wave 5 opens risk factors, analytics, graph risk mirror, and prediction for tier 2. A down child is left out of a live risk factor. Analytics, the mirror, and prediction throw. |
| 2026-11-16 | Wave 4 opens automation trigger, action, and fields for tier 2. Catalog rows leave on disable. A callback step errors when the addon is down. |
| 2026-11-16 | Tier 2 `registerLicenseFeatures` and `registerShutdownHook` stay closed. A shutdown hook can delay host shutdown. A license registration can overwrite catalog keys and mark `defaultAccess`. |
| 2026-11-16 | Wave 3 opens `registerFlaggable` for tier 2. `findUnique` and `findMany` call the child and throw when the child is down. |
| 2026-11-16 | Wave 2 opens approvable, approvable fields, and communicable for tier 2. `communicable` is a manifest extend id. Send and list use that owner. An unanswered approval callback stays pending. |
| 2026-11-16 | Wave 1 opens audit subject, record access, deletable, documentable, and linkable for tier 2. Notification types stay in the addon namespace. `registerCommunicable` stays refused. |
| 2026-11-16 | Tier 2 may call `ctx.core.communication.send`, `list` and `registerAccess`. Record access calls the child with `communication.access` and fails closed. |
| 2026-11-16 | Route-driven `ctx.data` writes record the forwarded HTTP user on `ADDON_DATA_WRITE`; jobs and events keep the addon service principal.                                   |
| 2026-11-16 | Host writes `ADDON_DATA_WRITE` on every tier 2 `ctx.data.execute` and on each execute statement in `ctx.data.transaction`.                                              |
| 2026-11-16 | Tier 2 `ctx.extend.*` registers only points named in manifest `extends`. Callbacks use `extend.callback`, the acting principal, and `addons.capabilities.timeoutMs`. A disabled, crashed, or slow child fails closed. |
| 2026-11-16 | Container runner dials pre-started containers over TCP. No Docker socket. Network policy allows only RPC port 7400 and the egress proxy on 7401. The process runner stays the default until `KASSIS_TIER2_CONTAINER_RUNNERS` is set. |
| 2026-11-16 | Process runner uses the Node permission model. Isolation is accident isolation: secret reads and spawn are denied; a TCP socket stays open on Node 24. `kassis-addon` is used only when the supervisor is root. |
| 2026-11-16 | Tier 2 `ctx.data.query`, `ctx.data.execute` and `ctx.data.transaction` run parameterised SQL as `addon_<id>_runtime`. Timeout and row cap come from Settings.            |
| 2026-11-16 | `@kassis/addon-sdk` types `ctx.data` as `AddonTier2DataClient` or `AddonTier1DataClient` from manifest `tier`; Prisma helpers are tier 1 only.                            |
| 2026-11-16 | Tier 2 supervision goes through `Tier2Runner` (`start`, `stop`, `call`, `health`). The current child process is the process runner.                                      |
| 2026-11-16 | Tier 2 may provide a namespaced capability declared in `provides`. Consumer calls are forwarded to the provider child with `addons.capabilities.timeoutMs`. A down provider returns null. |
| 2026-11-16 | Documented `@kassis/addon-sdk/tier-matrix.json` as the packaged tier capability matrix; CI checks it against `TIER2_FACADE_METHODS`.                                      |
| 2026-11-16 | `kassis-addon doctor --requirements` scans addon source for `ctx` calls the manifest tier cannot use and reports KADK-219 before build.                                    |
| 2026-10-28 | Tier 2 calls the host facades over RPC. Events and jobs are delivered to the child and retried on the existing queues. The child cannot call `approvals.applyRegistered`. |

# @kassis/addon-sdk

The public contract between a Kassis addon and the host:

- `AddonContext` v1: the only object an addon receives, bound to its id (types only; the host implements it from Phase 3b).
- Manifest v2: a JSON Schema (`schema/addon-manifest.v2.schema.json`), the `AddonManifestV2` type, and `validateManifestV2()`.
- `KADK` error codes: a data catalog (`codes/kadk-codes.json`) with a typed accessor. Every code is documented in [docs/developer/reference/adk-error-codes.md](../../docs/developer/reference/adk-error-codes.md).
- Tier capability matrix (`tier-matrix.json`): each `ctx` facade method with `tier1`, `tier2`, and manifest or principal permission gates. `npm run ci:adk:tier-matrix` keeps tier 2 rows aligned with the host allow-list.
- Guardrail catalogue (`guardrails.json`): id, group (A–F), enforcement level (L1–L5), check, primary `KADK` code and fix hint. Coding profiles, `certify`, the dev MCP server and docs read this file. `npm run ci:adk:guardrails-catalog` keeps profile keys aligned with the catalogue and requires every blocking guardrail in the unsigned v3 draft to name that machine check. Group D soft budgets and group E engineering practice rows name machine check ids (`adk.thin-addon-budgets`, `adk.outbound-timeouts`, and related); `kassis-addon budgets` / `engineering` implement them.
- Banned dependency list (`banned-dependencies.json`): mail, scheduler, upload, file-storage, auth, database, UI kit, and LLM packages. `kassis-addon check` refuses them (KADK-221).
- Process packs (`schema/process-pack.schema.json`, `process-pack-kinds.json`): `process/` files listed by `process.packs[]`. `kassis-addon check` validates keys, references, permissions and record types with no host. A kind whose `schema` is null has no host JSON Schema; check warns and does not invent a body schema.

Tier 1 (first-party, in process) and tier 2 (client code, own process) addons compile against the same package. An addon does not know which tier it runs in.

## Rules

**Self-contained.** The package imports only its own files and the npm packages declared in its `package.json` (`ajv`). No `@/`, no `server/`, no relative path out of the package, no Node built-ins, and no other `@kassis/*` package. `npm run ci:packages:addon-sdk-boundary` enforces this in CI with no baseline. A `@kassis/*` package can be allowed only after checking that it is self-contained too, by adding it to `SELF_CONTAINED_KASSIS_PACKAGES` in `tools/ci/check-addon-sdk-boundary.mjs`. Listed packages pass that check before they are added.

**Versioning.** The npm package is `0.1.0` and moves with the kit changesets group (`@kassis/adk-core`, `@kassis/mcp-contract`, `@kassis/addon-cli`, `@kassis/addon-testkit`). That number is not the host API. `HOST_API_VERSION` stays `1.0.0`, and addon manifests keep `hostApi` `^1.0.0`. A breaking host contract needs a new host API major. A breaking change to this package's public exports is a major of the kit group. New optional fields, facades and codes are minor releases; a deprecated API keeps working for at least one minor release. The package publishes publicly to npmjs.com (`publishConfig.registry` is `https://registry.npmjs.org/`). The published entry is JavaScript in `dist`. Inside this repository the `development` export condition still resolves `src`.

**Stable codes.** A published `KADK` code keeps its number, category and meaning. A retired code is marked retired in the catalog and the docs page; its number is never reused. New codes take the next free number in their range: 1xx manifest, 2xx boundaries, 3xx data, 4xx events, 5xx UI, 6xx security, 7xx attestation.

**One definition per shape.** Where the host has the same registration shape, the host type is the SDK type plus `addonName`, through a type-only import (for example `CapabilityRegistrationInput = CapabilityProvision & { addonName: string }`). Contribution types marked "host-specific" differ from the host's because the host uses Prisma or untyped values; the host adapts them in 3b.

## Using the context

```ts
import type { AddonContext, AddonManifestV2, DeclareAddon } from '@kassis/addon-sdk';

export const manifest = {
  manifestVersion: 2,
  id: 'sample-tprm-check' /* … */,
} as const satisfies AddonManifestV2;

type Declarations = DeclareAddon<
  typeof manifest,
  {
    publishes: { 'sample-tprm-check.assessment.completed': { partyId: string; score: number } };
    subscribes: { 'party.updated': { partyId: string } };
  }
>;

export async function initialize(ctx: AddonContext<Declarations>): Promise<void> {
  ctx.events.subscribe('party.updated', async (event) => {
    await ctx.audit.record(event.principal, 'sample-tprm-check.assessment.run', {
      subject: { type: 'party', id: event.payload.partyId },
    });
  });
}
```

With declarations, an undeclared event, audit action, job type, prompt key, secret key, route permission or capability does not compile. Without them every name is a `string`; the host checks the manifest at runtime either way. Declare payload types with `type`, not `interface`.

Contract rules built into the types:

- No method takes an addon name. The host binds identity.
- Every registration returns a `Disposable`. Registrations complete before the addon is marked ready, so a failed registration fails `initialize()`.
- Every operation on core data takes an `AddonPrincipal`. Only the host issues principals: `ctx.routes.principalOf(request)` in a route, `event.principal` and `job.principal` (the addon's service principal) in handlers. Facades check that principal's permissions and tenant.
- Every facade operation is async, so tier 2 can implement it over RPC. `ctx.capabilities.consume` returns `C | null`, and every caller handles `null`.
- `ctx.llm.invoke` takes a declared prompt key and variables. Model, provider, temperature, token limits and timeouts come from AI Settings and the prompt template; the host tags usage with the addon id.
- `ctx.audit.record` has no best-effort variant. It rejects when the record cannot be written.

## Facades and the host keys they replace

Evidence: `rg` over `addons/*/src` (and `dist` files with no `src` counterpart) for each key of table 5.3 in `docs/plans/completed/ADK-framework.md` and the methods called on it, on `feature/adk-framework` after phase 2c. Only operations in real use are in the contract.

They are internal wiring or capabilities, not core facades. control-room calls aml-services-core's `jurisdictionService`; that becomes a capability.
- `aiConfig`: model selection stays in AI Settings (C9). investigation-panel reads the model name only for token budgeting; `llm.estimateTokens` and `LlmResult.model` cover it.

## The 38 host `register*` methods
